USER_SUSPENDED and other account notices stay non-link rows. - #answer- scroll and flash: AnswerHashFlash (inside AnswersSection) runs on load, hashchange and popstate. lib/locationEvents.js patches history.pushState and replaceState to emit "app:locationchange", because a Next that only changes the hash fires neither event. lib/flash.js holds the ring flash shared with the best answer "View in list" control, and honors prefers-reduced-motion.

Batch 4, reports. - ReportsDashboard: content_exists false shows "Content removed" and hides Resolve & delete (plain resolve and reject stay). A DELETE_CONTENT resolve with auto_resolved_count above zero shows a dismissible notice and refetches page one silently. Content-type select and the escalated filter combine with the status tabs. A request counter drops stale list responses, load-more is guarded the same way. Delete now has an inline confirmation because it cascades to answers, comments and other reports. - /my-reports: server wrapper (noindex metadata) around MyReportsClient, GET /reports/mine/ with All, Pending, Reviewed and No action taken tabs. Never shows reviewer or escalation data. Disallowed in robots.js. Linked from ProfileMenu, deliberately not from the profile page or tabs. - lib/reportLabels.js holds the report type labels shared by both screens.

Batch 5, admin, moderation and profile. - Hub offline: HubStatusControl lives in AdminHubPicker, not on school rows, because an offline hub reports has_hub false and would look the same as no hub. SchoolPicker gained onlyWithHub (default true) so the admin picker can search every school, then GET /hubs/by-school/{id}/, which admins can read while a hub is offline. An offline hub hides HubTeamManager since its moderator and representative routes 404. Only taking offline asks for confirmation. refreshUser() runs after a change because /users/me/ lists only active hubs. - SchoolsManager: Active, Inactive, All tabs. A row whose toggle moves it out of the current view is removed locally and the count adjusted. - ActivationRequestsQueue: rejection reason shown on rows, reject input capped at 1000 with a remaining counter, a 400 surfaces under the field. - UserSearchPicker: excludeIds is keyed by its joined ids so the search callback stays stable, 429 gets its own copy, results disable while an add is in flight. TeamMemberList uses a ref guard against double submits. - Profile: section order swapped (no fetch ordering dependency existed), name edit trimmed and validated, avatar alt empty with no-referrer. FormControls gained an lg size for the name field.

Batch 6 and follow-ups. - Tags: /tags and TagsManager paginate with load-more (deduped by id because popularity order can shift between pages), TagsManager keeps the search bar mounted while loading. Suggestion lists use page_size=10 and drop stale responses. sitemap.js uses one fetchAll helper (schools 10x100, tags 10x100, questions 25x50) that keeps partial results and lists the slugged canonical school URL. - Load-more guards: RecentQuestionsList uses a mounted ref, the search page uses a load counter plus a mounted ref, so a late "View more" can no longer append stale rows. - SchoolPicker gained notice and busyId props, so feedback about a pick renders under that school's row. - ThemeToggle is a TopBar icon button, icons swapped with CSS dark: variants instead of state so the icon never flashes wrong, storage access wrapped in try/catch. The sidebar footer was removed. - Profile: components/ui/Tabs.js (accessible tablist, arrow keys, scrolls instead of wrapping), identity card with stats strip, one tab strip that merges recent activity and post history. PostHistoryTabs was deleted. - Open: moderators are not told when their hub goes offline because GET /users/me/ omits it. Backend issue drafted, frontend half waits for it.

Batch 7, UX leftovers. - Contrast: text-gray-400 (about 2.5:1 light) and text-gray-500 (about 3.7:1 dark) failed AA. New --color-muted token (light #67645C, dark #9EA1AB) and a text-muted utility, swapped in with a perl sweep. The border-strong tokens measure about 1.6:1 against a 3:1 target for field edges, left unchanged by choice, candidate values noted in the feature list. - AskFab (mobile only, signed in, hidden on forms and staff tools) at z-sticky, AppShell main gained bottom padding on mobile. - Primitives sweep by scripts/codemod-primitives.mjs (dry run by default): ErrorMessage for red and amber paragraphs with a size class, Input, Select and Textarea for controls with the standard styling. Skips are listed, checkboxes and radios silently. It restyles, it does not wire labels. - lib/formErrors.js turns DRF field-keyed 400s into per-field messages. The ask, edit, answer, department and request-hub forms use FormField plus it. SchoolPicker's notice and busyId now also serve the ask form. - MarkdownEditor: word and character count in richMode, real accessible names on toolbar buttons, id, invalid, aria-describedby and aria-label props so FormField can wire it.

Batch 8, shared patterns. - IconLabel (xs, sm, md) owns icon size and text size for every meta row, adopted in the question meta row, answer and comment bylines and SchoolMetaBadge. The school hero rows already match md and were left. - EmptyState adopted in the lists a user can land on (hub, tag and school lists, departments, profile tabs, unanswered queue, users, pages). - Load-more failures now show on the three profile tabs and UnansweredQueue. - ReportButton and EscalateButton use FormField. The school filters do too. - CommentThread's post box is an Input with an accessible name.

docs.title: Frontend Design Decisions
docs.text:
• Light and dark themes shipped together, with a manual toggle persisted in localStorage.
  • A single blue accent (#2563eb) is defined as a CSS variable; the rest of the palette remains restrained and neutral.
  • Styling uses custom Tailwind utilities rather than a third-party component library.
  • Structural chrome shares the page background tokens. Elevated popovers are the deliberate exception.
  • --color-border is for dividers and edges, --color-border-strong for controls, and named z-index utilities from globals.css for overlays.
  • --color-muted is the shared token for secondary text.

docs.title: Current Phase
docs.text: Mobile MVP built by an AI agent from Mobile_mockup.html, working against the live API. The post-MVP audit (M0 to M13, B1 branding, G1 native Google sign in) is complete. Remaining before launch: verify the final preview build on devices (see DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md). iOS items are implemented and untested.

docs.title: Completed
docs.text: • Agent build: every screen, verified in Expo web at 390x844 against the live API (2026-11-10)

docs.title: Mobile Audit Pass (Post-MVP)
docs.text:
Test device: Android 9. iOS items are implemented but left unchecked in feature-list.md as untested.

M0, context and parity matrix. No code. Found doc errors in mobile-map.md (endpoint names and mockup path), confirmed against src/api/endpoints.ts that the client itself was already correct.

M1, bugs and missing actions. - Lock and unlock: root cause was lockedNow = locked || question.is_locked. Once the loaded question was locked, the stale is_locked kept the button on Unlock even after a successful unlock. locked is now the only source of truth, synced from the question in the existing effect. Added an in-flight guard (lockBusy) and dev-only logging of the request method and response. - Comments: new CommentsSheet (src/features/comments) with a per-comment action menu. Own comments get Edit and Delete, other people's get Report, hub staff also get Escalate. api.comments.update already existed, only the UI was missing. Menu, edit, delete and report all render inside the one sheet by mode, no stacked Modals. Hardware Back steps back to the thread first and closes the sheet only from the thread. - Comment thread has its own post error (a failed post no longer replaces the thread), View more pagination (page_size 20, deduped by id), and a stale-response guard. Answer comment_count is kept in sync through an onCountChange callback. - Report and escalate extracted into a shared ReportForm (src/features/reports) used by the question and answer menus and by comments. Escalate stays one button: POST /reports/ then POST /reports/{id}/escalate/, "already reported" shows the admin-will-review copy.

M2a, keyboard foundation, part 1. - New src/lib/useKeyboard.ts, the single source of keyboard state. Sheet adopted it. No behavior change. QuestionScreen and MarkdownEditor adopt it in M2b.

M2b, keyboard foundation, part 2. - Device finding (Android 9): the composer and the Ask form were hidden by the keyboard because QuestionScreen and AskScreen passed no behavior to KeyboardAvoidingView on Android, while sheets (behavior "height") worked. New components/KeyboardAvoid.tsx is the one wrapper for screens with inputs: 'height' on Android, 'padding' with a safe area plus top bar offset on iOS (iOS untested). - QuestionScreen and AskScreen use useKeyboard (listeners removed). The Ask tags input scrolls to the end on focus because it is the last field. - QuestionScreen split: new features/answers/AnswerCard, AnswerComposer (owns its draft, post and keyboard padding) and BestAnswerPin. The screen is about half the size. - Known follow-up: the composer editor has no maxHeight, long text can squeeze the screen while the keyboard is up. Handled in M3 with the editor rewrite.

Platform badge parity. - New components/PlatformBadge.tsx (PlatformBadge and OfficialAccountNote). The badge now shows on the question author, best answer pin, answer bylines and comments, matching the web. Inside the comments sheet the tap opens an inline note (no stacked Modal). Other surfaces that show an author (QuestionRow, notifications, profile) are checked in their own passes.

M4, question share text (folded into M2b, QuestionScreen was already open). - Share message is title, then "Status, N answers, N views", then WEB_BASE_URL/questions/{id}/{slug} (slug omitted if missing).

M3, markdown editor v2, renderer parity and tag search. - MarkdownEditor rewritten. Toolbar buttons are 44pt in a horizontally scrollable bar with Preview pinned at the right, and the toolbar can dock under the input (toolbar="bottom", used by the answer composer) so it stays next to the keyboard. The input has maxHeight with internal scroll. Editing logic is pure functions in src/lib/markdownEdit.ts: toggle inline formatting off (also when the cursor sits inside the markers), toggle block prefixes per line, link wrapping that selects the part the user types next, and list continuation. Continuation runs in onChangeText by diffing for an inserted newline, because onKeyPress Enter is unreliable on Android soft keyboards. The cursor is placed by a forced selection prop that is released after the native selection event (or 400 ms). Italic uses _ like the web. Preview uses the display Markdown component. - Markdown renderer parity with the web (marked plus sanitize-html): nested lists, ordered list start numbers, consecutive quote lines merged into one block, bare URL autolinks, mailto links, backslash escapes, intraword underscores stay plain, images are dropped, unsafe link schemes render as plain text, ~~~ fences. The inline parser is a small tokenizer instead of one split regex. parseMarkdown now returns nested list blocks. - New features/questions/TagInput (used by Ask): chips with remove, popular tags when focused and empty, 300 ms debounced search, free text via Done or a comma, 50 character limit. The list renders inline under the field so it works inside the form ScrollView. Ask scrolls the field to the top of the viewport when it gets focus. - ModalSheet.tsx (Dialog, ActionMenu) deleted, nothing imported it.

M3 follow-up. TextInputSelectionChangeEvent is not exported by RN 0.88.1, MarkdownEditor uses the public TextInputSelectionChangeEvent type instead (NativeSyntheticEvent import removed). Mailto links stay plain text on mobile, the web autolinks them, accepted difference.

M5, shell and cross-cutting. - App.tsx: useFonts error no longer leaves a blank screen, the pre-font screen uses the palette for the system scheme (no white flash in dark mode), the app is wrapped in the new components/ErrorBoundary (friendly fallback, Try again, componentDidCatch is the crash reporting hook). - TabBar matches the mockup (no ring around Ask, 56pt slots, raised 20pt, unread count in the accessibility label). Drawer closes with a swipe left (PanResponder drives the same Animated value), uses useWindowDimensions, announces as a modal. - QuestionRow snippets go through lib/stripMarkdown (port of the web function). - Markdown allowHeadings now defaults to false like the web, PageScreen passes true. Closes the M3 backlog item, no Q&A call site needs a change. - OfflineBanner copy no longer claims saved content, nothing is cached yet (offline cache is an M12 decision). - Findings moved to backlog: linking config (M12), legacy palette aliases, SkeletonBlock width typing, theme preference flash, reduced motion, pruning admin methods from endpoints.ts (M12), SecureStore size limit for the cached user (M6), pluralize in QuestionScreen (M9).

M6, auth and session. - Startup: a failed GET /users/me/ keeps the session and starts from the cached user unless it was a definitive 401 (network, timeout, 429 and 5xx used to clear the tokens). - The unauthorized handler only raises the session-expired sheet when a session existed. - Seeded dev tokens and the developer token sheet are DEV only, so preview and production builds never contain a login bypass. - Google sign in: native uses the authorization code flow with PKCE (the provider exchanges the code, needs expo-crypto), web keeps the token flow. Android and iOS OAuth clients do not support the implicit flow. Unverified on a device until the first EAS build. - StaffDrawerSection indent fixed.

B1, branding and identifiers. - Identifiers set: com.brandnova.academiaatlas (Android and iOS), scheme academiaatlas, slug academia-atlas-mobile, launcher name A-Atlas (store titles say Academia Atlas). - brand/src holds the four design exports, scripts/make-brand-assets.sh generates the icon, adaptive foreground and monochrome, splash light and dark, favicon, store, consent and web icons with ImageMagick. config/brand.ts and components/BrandMark are the only places the logo is referenced in code. TopBar and BootSplash use them, Login too. - expo-splash-screen plugin with light and dark backgrounds. eas.json added (development, preview, production). - Removed unused TopBar helpers DetailTopBar, CircleButton, BackLink. - Storage keys keep the academia. prefix. User-facing strings were renamed by sed.

B1 follow-up. BrandMark falls back to an aspect ratio of 1 when Image.resolveAssetSource returns no size (strict typing).

M7, home, search, schools and tags. - New shared Chip and FilterChips (components/Chips.tsx, variants solid, outline, plain, horizontal scroll or wrap, allowClear), used by Schools, Search and Tag questions. The School screen adopts them in M8. Chips.tsx moved onto the token names (no legacy aliases). - New features/schools/SchoolCard (Home strip): icon tile, short name, full name, location, live question count. Hub counts keep one GET /hubs/by-school/{id}/ per card (at most 5, the backend caches hub detail for 60 s) and now refresh with pull to refresh and on tab focus. Backend issue 1 asks for hub_question_count on the schools list instead. - New features/tags/TagFilter (Search): selected tag chip with x, popular chips, "More tags" sheet with debounced search and View more. Replaces six fixed chips. - Schools gained the state filter (free text, 500 ms debounce, exact match like the web). Tags gained a Popular or A to Z order. Counts no longer flash 0 while loading, Search shows "Searching..." during the debounce, results close the keyboard on drag. - The Search 5xx fallback to GET /questions/ is now DEV only, so a production outage is not hidden behind unranked results. - Backend issues raised, not changed here: hub_question_count on GET /schools/, answer_count and department on GET /search/questions/ rows.

M7 follow-up. Home school cards redesigned (SchoolCard: tile, large question count top right, short name, two-line name, location and chevron footer). The tile is where a per-school logo goes after launch.

First preview build findings (Android 9). - EAS never reads .env (git-ignored), so the build had no EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL (a release build falls back to 10.0.2.2:8000, unreachable) and no Google client ids. Public values now live in eas.json env blocks per profile. - The native splash rendered the 1024 px image oversize. The native splash is now colour only (light and dark), the JS boot screen shows the logo. Image splash can return with a small test asset. - The dev build failed to install (storage). Expo Go covers JS work, the preview build covers native Google sign in.

M8 and M9, questions, ask, answers. - Ask: editing always loads the question fresh (the old useQuery plus hydrate guard re-showed pre-edit text and skipped reloading the same id). Loading and error states added. - Question: the school in the meta row opens the school page (web breadcrumb parity). Vote switching updates the UI after each confirmed server step, so a failure on the second call leaves a correct state. Local count helper replaced by pluralize. - School: ordering control (Newest, Oldest, Most viewed, Least viewed), FilterChips, hero and request sheet extracted to features/schools/SchoolHero and RequestHubSheet.

M10, notifications and my reports. - Notifications refetch when the tab regains focus, rows announce Unread, filters use FilterChips. All 12 types have an icon, link_target and admin web handoffs verified. My reports uses FilterChips, privacy rules verified (no reviewer or escalation data).

Dev access. - features/auth/DevAccessSheet is shared by Login and the sign-in sheet (development builds only). Login shows only for a first-time guest or after logout, so the sheet is now also reachable from any sign-in prompt.

M11, profile, my reports and pages. - Profile: the three lists (questions, answers, comments) live in features/profile/useProfileActivity and each tab pages with View more. Activity merges the newest 20. ProfileTabs, EditNameSheet and a reusable components/Tabs (underlined, scrolling) replace the 470 line screen. - Pages list: pull to refresh and Staff and Draft badges (the API returns them to staff and admins). - BrandMark sizes with explicit width and height (an aspectRatio only layout rendered the logo at its pixel size in release builds).

Google sign in findings (preview build). - "Access blocked, custom scheme" on Android 15: the build used the web client id because the Android client id was missing. Native sign in needs an Android client (package plus SHA-1 of the signing key, custom URI scheme enabled). app.json scheme is now an array including the package name so the redirect has an intent filter. Android 9 crashed natively, trace pending. A native Google account picker is the fallback. - Play re-signs the app, so the production profile needs a second Android client for the Play signing SHA-1.

M12, cross-cutting. - Deep links: navigation/linking.ts with the academiaatlas:// scheme, the web URL as a prefix and paths that mirror the web routes (schools/:id/:slug?, questions/:id/:slug?, tags/:tag, pages/:slug and more). A #answer-{id} suffix opens the question scrolled to that answer. https links still need Android intent filters (autoVerify) and assetlinks.json on the final domain, tracked in DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST. - endpoints.ts pruned to the user client (no admin, moderation, school or tag management, unanswered queue). - Legacy palette aliases removed from the theme and every component. Form inputs and the editor container use the strong border token per design-guide. The theme provider holds the first paint until the stored preference is read. - Reduced motion (lib/useReduceMotion) stops the skeleton pulse. Text scaling is capped at 1.4. Error states and form errors have the alert role. ErrorState has a "Can't connect" variant for network errors. - Decision: no offline content cache before launch. It needs a storage dependency and an invalidation plan, tracked as a future item with the web's low-data mode. The banner copy stays honest. - BrandMark uses a constant ratio of 1 and the brand PNGs are generated square, because Image.resolveAssetSource is not reliable on Expo web.

G1, native Google sign in. - Android 9 crash trace: expo-web-browser picked an installed app's non-exported WebView activity (OPay merchant) as the browser for the Google redirect, which Android rejects with a SecurityException. A browser redirect login depends on whatever browsers the phone exposes, so native sign in moved to the native Google account picker (@react-native-google-signin/google-signin). - GoogleSignInButton: native uses GoogleSignin (hasPlayServices, signOut to force the chooser, signIn, getTokens), the backend contract is unchanged (access token to POST /auth/google/). Web keeps the expo-auth-session token flow with the web client id. Expo Go has no native module, the button explains that and Developer access remains the way in. The Android client is matched by package and SHA-1, no id in code, EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_ID is retired. The scheme array is no longer needed. - TopBar wordmark never wraps (one line, shrinks to 80 percent, font scale capped at 1.1).

M13, docs sync and final checklists. - mobile-map.md rewritten at the frontend-map depth (props, endpoints per screen, endpoint index). - feature-list.md Mobile section rewritten (no em dashes, same area headings as the web), TESTING.md Mobile section consolidated into the final regression checklist, CHANGELOG entry added. - Brand sources and the asset generator move to the repo root (brand/), they serve web and mobile.

docs.title: Key Decisions (append)
docs.text:
• Comment actions, report and escalate live inside one sheet and switch by mode, because stacked Modals are unreliable on older Android
  • canModerateHub (admin, moderator or representative of the hub) is the single check for lock and escalate, matching the contract
  • Keyboard handling goes through one hook, the strategy per platform is decided from device results in M2b
  • One KeyboardAvoid wrapper per screen with inputs, one useKeyboard hook for keyboard state. No Keyboard.addListener anywhere else
  • Reused UI lives in components or features folders, screens compose them. Extract on sight when a block is used twice or makes a screen long
  • Badge tap in a sheet shows its note inline, never a second Modal
  • Editing helpers are pure functions in lib/markdownEdit.ts, the editor component only wires them to the TextInput
  • List continuation is detected from the text change, never from key events
  • Suggestion lists render inline in the form, not as an absolute popover, so they work inside ScrollViews on older Android
  • Markdown allowHeadings defaults to true until the Q&A call sites pass false (matches the web, where only static pages render headings). Tracked in feature-list.md
  • Branding: the logo concept is traced to three master SVGs (brand/src) and every PNG (icon, adaptive foreground and monochrome, splash light and dark, favicon, store and web sizes) is generated by scripts/make-brand-assets.sh, never cropped from the JPEG
  • Identifiers (Android package, iOS bundle id, URL scheme, EAS slug) are decided before the first EAS build because the Android package is permanent after the first Play upload. Pending decision, recommended com.brandnova.academiaatlas, scheme academiaatlas, slug academia-atlas-mobile. The UI accent stays #3454D1, logo navy and gold are brand colors for icons, splash and store graphics only
  • The folder rename academia-mobile to mobile waits until after M13, with the web rename
  • Storage keys keep the academia. prefix (renaming would sign users out)
  • Dev tooling (dev token sheet, seeded tokens) is compiled out of release builds by DEV
  • The UI accent #3454D1 is also the logo blue, gold is used only in the logo
  • The launcher label is the short name A-Atlas, store titles use Academia Atlas
  • Home hub counts: keep the per-card request (bounded at 5, cached on the backend) until the backend adds hub_question_count to the schools list
  • One Chip component for every filter or tag chip, screens never hand-roll chip styles
  • Search fallback to the plain question filter exists in development builds only
  • Public build configuration lives in eas.json env per profile, never in .env
  • Native splash is colour only until an image splash is verified on a device
  • Vote UI state always mirrors the last confirmed server step
  • The Login screen stays a one-time welcome, the sign-in sheet and drawer are the entry points until email and password auth exists
  • The default backend server stays the default. LAN access is opt-in (make run-lan), adb reverse or a deployed backend are the alternatives
  • The mobile client carries no admin or moderation API methods, staff tools are web only
  • No offline content cache before launch (banner only)
  • Brand mark PNGs are square so layout never depends on an image ratio
  • Native Google sign in uses the native account picker, not a browser redirect (reliability across phones). The preview build is the only build needed for it, no development build is required for the MVP
  • Builds are budgeted, pre-flight (typecheck, expo-doctor, export, prebuild) runs before every EAS build

docs.title: Known Deviations From Docs (Mobile)
docs.text:
• mobile-map.md listed the cached user key as academia.cached_user, the code uses academia.user (doc fixed).
  • endpoints.ts contains admin and moderation methods the user client never calls (prune in M12).

Run against the live Postgres-backed API at 390x844:

  • Invalid access plus valid refresh made exactly one refresh call and retried the original request. Invalid refresh cleared the session and showed the expired-session sheet over the current screen.
  • Guest: Login, Browse as a guest, guest drawer, sign-in sheet and guest ask sheet all worked.
  • Dev token: the Login sheet accepted a seeded user token and reached Home.
  • Home: loaded 18 schools, hub question counts, popular tags and recent questions. View more requested page 2 and appended without duplicates.
  • Search: a 500 ms debounce, tag filter and result count worked. After the backend rank fix, a specific query returned 7 relevant rows.
  • Schools: search, has-hub filter and filter count worked. The request included has_hub=true.
  • School: ABU rendered details, hub counts, status and department filters. BUK showed the no-hub card and the activation request sheet. Starting Ask from a school prefilled the form.
  • Ask: empty submit showed the title field error. Filling title, body and tags returned 201, opened the new question, and the question was deleted with 204.
  • Question: solved question showed the best answer pin; View in list scrolled to the answer. Follow, kebab actions, report sheet and escalate sheet rendered.
  • Answers: a vote was added and removed, a comment was posted, and an answer was posted. The comment and answer were deleted after the check.
  • Mark best: a temporary question and answer were created; marking best changed the status to SOLVED and showed the pin. The question was then deleted with 404 on the follow-up GET.
  • Lock: staff lock and unlock made POST and DELETE requests and both returned
  • The question was restored.
  • Notifications: filters, unread tint, read marking, deep link to the linked question and admin web action rendered. The clicked notification was restored to unread after the test.
  • Profile: activity, questions, answers and comments tabs loaded the expected endpoints. Edit name disabled Save when blank and PATCHed the name. The name was restored.
  • My reports, pages, page view, staff web handoff, offline banner and dark mode were all screenshotted and checked.
  • No console or page errors were observed in the final checks.

docs.title: Deployment Checklist
docs.text:
One checklist for the whole launch. Work through Backend, then Web, then Mobile, then the shared operations and runbook at the end. Day-to-day regression checks are in TESTING.md. Provider-account steps need access to those accounts.

[ ] not done, [x] done. Commands assume Fedora bash.

docs.title: 0. Before anything else
docs.text:
• [ ] Domain and DNS decided (web, API, optional status page).
  • [ ] Support inbox exists and is monitored (it is shown to suspended users and in store listings).
  • [ ] Password manager holds every secret below, never git or chat.
  • [ ] Accounts exist: Vercel, Supabase, Upstash, email provider, Google Cloud, Expo (EAS), Apple Developer, Google Play Console.
  • [ ] Rollback owner and launch day decided (avoid launching on a Friday evening).

docs.title: 1.1 Environment and secrets
docs.text:
• [ ] SECRET_KEY is new, long and unique per environment.
  • [ ] DEBUG is off. print_test_tokens refuses to run, confirm it does.
  • [ ] DATABASE_URL is set and scoped to every environment that builds or runs (the production settings guard also fires during Vercel builds). DJANGO_ALLOW_SQLITE is NOT set in production.
  • [ ] DATABASE_CONN_MAX_AGE=0 behind the Supabase transaction pooler.
  • [ ] ALLOWED_HOSTS, CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS and CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS list exact origins, no wildcards. The Expo web preview origin is absent from production.
  • [ ] FRONTEND_URL is the live site, so email buttons link correctly.
  • [ ] REDIS_URL points at Upstash. Cache TTL variables reviewed.
  • [ ] Email delivery variables are set for the real provider (not MailHog).

docs.title: 1.2 Database
docs.text:
• [ ] Production Postgres created, backups enabled, point-in-time recovery understood.
  • [ ] python manage.py migrate applied. makemigrations --check shows nothing pending.
  • [ ] Django admin superuser created with a strong password. Admin URL protected (consider restricting or renaming the path).
  • [ ] A platform admin account exists (and the platform account used for seed content, see 1.6).

docs.title: 1.3 Security and platform
docs.text:
• [ ] HTTPS only. HSTS, secure cookies and SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER are active in production settings.
  • [ ] Browsable API renderer is disabled (responses are JSON only).
  • [ ] makemigrations, check --deploy run clean: python manage.py check --deploy
  • [ ] Static files served (whitenoise) and Django admin loads with styling.
  • [ ] No secrets in the repo: git log -p | grep -iE "secret|password|token" reviewed.

docs.title: 1.4 Cache and throttling
docs.text:
• [ ] Throttle counters use the shared Redis, not per-process memory.
  • [ ] Redis outage fails open (kill the connection once on a preview and confirm the API still answers).
  • [ ] Rate limits behave on the live API (see 1.7).

docs.title: 1.5 Email
docs.text:
• [ ] Send each emailed notification once with real accounts: new answer, best answer, hub activated, hub rejected (with reason), account suspended. Check the inbox, spam folder and links.
  • [ ] Sender domain has SPF and DKIM so mail does not land in spam.

docs.title: 1.6 Data and accounts
docs.text:
• [ ] School directory imported with import_school_directory. New schools import inactive: review and activate them deliberately. known_possible_duplicates.csv triaged.
  • [ ] Never run seed_demo_data --clear against production (it wipes schools).
  • [ ] Static pages created through the admin: Privacy Policy, Terms, Community Guidelines (public) and the Moderator Handbook (staff), all published.
  • [ ] Platform (official) account created, promoted to admin, its id noted for the frontend and mobile PLATFORM_ACCOUNT_ID variables, before seed questions are posted.
  • [ ] First hubs activated, first representatives and moderators assigned.

docs.title: 1.7 API smoke tests
docs.text:
API=https://YOUR-BACKEND/api/v1
curl -s $API/health/ | python -m json.tool                       # status ok, database ok, cache ok
curl -s "$API/schools/?page_size=2" | python -m json.tool | head -20
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" $API/users/me/          # 401
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" $API/nope/              # 404 as JSON, not an HTML page
curl -s "$API/search/questions/?q=zzqx+wwvk" | python -m json.tool | head -5   # count 0 (rank floor)
curl -s -I -H "Origin: https://evil.example" $API/schools/ | grep -i access-control   # prints nothing
for i in $(seq 1 12); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} " -X POST $API/auth/google/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"access_token":"x"}'; done; echo   # 401s, then 429
  • [ ] All of the above behave as commented.
  • [ ] Token refresh and refresh-token revocation work against the live API (log out, reuse the old refresh token).
  • [ ] A suspended account is rejected at login with the 403 message.

docs.title: 1.8 Permissions spot checks (live API, three test accounts)
docs.text:
• [ ] A regular user gets 403 on: schools POST, tag merge, report resolve, admin users, hub PATCH.
  • [ ] A moderator can lock a question in their hub and gets 403 in another hub.
  • [ ] A representative can assign a moderator for their hub only.
  • [ ] A guest can read but gets 401 on every write.

docs.title: 1.9 Observability and backups
docs.text:
• [ ] Error alerting (Sentry or equivalent) for the backend, with a test event received.
  • [ ] Uptime check on /api/v1/health/ with an alert route.
  • [ ] Database backup restore tested once, not just configured.
  • [ ] Log location known (Vercel logs), structured logs readable.

docs.title: 2.1 Environment (redeploy after changes, NEXT_PUBLIC_* is baked in at build)
docs.text:
• [ ] BACKEND_API_URL: the backend /api/v1 base, no trailing slash, server only.
  • [ ] NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: the real public origin. It is also used for the server's calls to its own proxy, so a wrong value breaks server-rendered pages.
  • [ ] NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.
  • [ ] NEXT_PUBLIC_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT_ID (optional, comma-separated).
  • [ ] Variables are scoped to Production, and Preview uses the preview backend.
  • [ ] Production branch is main. Preview deployments do not use production secrets.

docs.title: 2.2 Google sign in
docs.text:
• [ ] The production origin is in the OAuth client's Authorized JavaScript origins.
  • [ ] The consent screen is published, not in testing mode, or only test users can sign in.
  • [ ] Sign in works with a brand-new Google account, an existing account and a suspended account.

docs.title: 2.3 Session and proxy
docs.text:
• [ ] Cookies show HttpOnly and Secure on the live domain (DevTools, Application tab), SameSite Lax.
  • [ ] No token is visible to JavaScript (document.cookie shows no auth cookie).
  • [ ] After a long idle or backend cold start, a page loads or shows the friendly "taking too long" copy, never a raw 500.
  • [ ] Logging out blacklists the refresh token.

docs.title: 2.3b Build and quality gates
docs.text:
• [ ] npm run check && npm run build pass with no warnings you do not understand.
  • [ ] Lighthouse mobile on the home page, a school page and a question page. Note the scores, fix anything under 80 for performance or under 90 for accessibility.
  • [ ] Light and dark mode and a 360px width through: sign in, ask, answer, vote, comment, notifications, profile, report, search.
  • [ ] Keyboard-only pass: tab through a question page, every control reachable with a visible focus ring.
  • [ ] Browser matrix: latest Chrome, Safari (iOS), Firefox, Samsung Internet if you can.
  • [ ] 404 and error pages render for a missing school, question and page.

docs.title: 2.4 Search and sharing
docs.text:
• [ ] Add the property in Google Search Console (DNS domain verification is the least fiddly), submit /sitemap.xml, inspect the home page, a school, a question and a tag.
  • [ ] /robots.txt shows the disallow list, and /my-reports, /admin and /moderation are blocked.
  • [ ] Rich Results Test passes on a question (BreadcrumbList) and the home page (WebSite).
  • [ ] Facebook Sharing Debugger and the X card validator show correct cards for a school and a question.
  • [ ] Preview deployments are not indexable (check the response headers).
  • [ ] Canonical URLs use the real domain.

docs.title: 2.5 Content and legal
docs.text:
• [ ] Privacy Policy, Terms, Community Guidelines and the Moderator Handbook are published.
  • [ ] Footer links to them work. The app-promotion banner, if built, stays hidden until store URLs exist.

docs.title: 3.1 Brand and app identity
docs.text:
• [ ] OAuth clients created in Google Cloud: Web (also used for the web preview), Android for the EAS keystore (package com.brandnova.academiaatlas, SHA-1 from eas credentials, custom URI scheme enabled) and iOS (bundle id). Native sign in uses code flow with PKCE, so the Android and iOS clients need no secret.
  • [ ] After the first Play upload, create a second Android client for the Play app signing SHA-1 and put its id in the production profile.
  • [ ] Image splash re-introduced only after a small test asset renders correctly on a real device (native splash is colour only for now).
  • [ ] iOS bundle identifier and Android package name set in app.json (currently com.brandnova.academiaatlas).
  • [ ] Ownership of the academiaatlas URL scheme and any universal link domain confirmed.
  • [ ] Store screenshots at the required sizes for iPhone and Android.
  • [ ] Store descriptions, keywords and privacy answers written.
  • [x] Identifiers decided and set in app.json: com.brandnova.academiaatlas (Android and iOS), scheme academiaatlas, slug academia-atlas-mobile, launcher name A-Atlas. Google OAuth redirect URIs must be created from these.
  • [ ] Icon kit generated by brand/make-brand-assets.sh from brand/src and checked on a real build (icon, adaptive, monochrome, splash light and dark), plus Play 512, Google consent logo 120 and the Play feature graphic 1024x500 made by hand.
  • [ ] expo-splash-screen plugin configured with light and dark backgrounds and checked on Android 12+ and iOS (Android 9 shows the legacy splash).
  • [ ] Monochrome icon checked on Android 13+ themed icons, launcher label checked for truncation.
  • [ ] The production profile in eas.json holds the real production API, web URL and the production database's platform account id (no placeholders).

docs.title: 3.2 Expo and EAS
docs.text:
• [ ] Expo account and organization created, npx eas init run, placeholder ownership replaced.
  • [ ] EAS build profiles for development, preview and production.
  • [ ] Development build with the real identifiers, then a preview build for testers.
  • [ ] iOS certificates and Android keystores managed through EAS, stored in the password manager.
  • [ ] Decision on EAS Update (channels and a rollback plan if yes).
  • [ ] Crash reporting (Sentry or equivalent) added before the first tester build. If added, wire it into ErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch.
  • [ ] Pre-flight before every EAS build: typecheck, expo-doctor, npx expo export --platform android, npx expo prebuild --platform android --no-install --clean then rm -rf android.
  • [ ] Build budget tracked (free tier, local builds with eas build --local do not use cloud builds). Decision on EAS Update (expo-updates, runtimeVersion) made before the last native build.

docs.title: 3.3 Google sign in
docs.text:
• [ ] OAuth clients in one Google Cloud project: Web (its id goes in EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID), Android (package com.brandnova.academiaatlas plus the SHA-1 of the EAS keystore from eas credentials -p android, no id goes in the app), iOS later.
  • [ ] After the first Play upload add a second Android client with the Play app signing SHA-1 (Play re-signs the app).
  • [ ] Consent screen branding (name, support email, 120px logo). While in Testing, add test users, switch to In production to open it up.
  • [ ] Native sign in verified on a real Android 9 and Android 15 phone and an iPhone: new account, existing account, suspended account (403 copy and support email visible), cancelled chooser.
  • [ ] No client secret exists anywhere in the mobile project.

docs.title: 3.4 API and configuration
docs.text:
• [ ] EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL (https, including /api/v1), EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_BASE_URL and the Google client ids are set in the eas.json env block of every profile you build (EAS never reads the local .env). A build without EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL silently targets 10.0.2.2, and the web base URL defaults to the preview site.
  • [ ] The backend health URL opens in the phone's browser before you build.
  • [ ] No test tokens, .env files or keystores are committed.
  • [ ] Tokens are only in SecureStore on device, never AsyncStorage.
  • [ ] Token refresh verified against production with an expired access token, and a network failure during refresh does not sign the user out.
  • [ ] Backend revokes the refresh token on logout.
  • [ ] The search rank-floor fix is deployed (the mobile Search screen depends on it).
  • [ ] EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL (https), EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_BASE_URL and the Google client ids are set for each EAS profile. A build without EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL silently targets localhost or 10.0.2.2, and the web base URL defaults to the preview site.
  • [ ] Preview builds use an https backend (Android 9 and newer block cleartext HTTP in release builds).
  • [ ] Dev token sheet cannot appear in preview or production builds (compiled out by DEV), confirm once on a preview APK.

docs.title: 3.5 Permissions, privacy and store compliance
docs.text:
• [ ] app.json and the built manifest request no permissions beyond network access (no location, camera, photos, contacts or microphone), matching the Privacy Policy.
  • [ ] No analytics or advertising SDK in the app. Any crash reporting is disclosed.
  • [ ] Privacy Policy page covers the mobile app (secure storage, Google sign in) and its URL is entered in both stores.
  • [ ] Apple privacy nutrition labels and the Google Data safety form completed and consistent with the policy.
  • [ ] Account deletion: both stores require apps that create accounts to provide a way to request deletion (Apple: a path inside the app, Google: an in-app path plus a web link). Decide the path (a "Request account deletion" action that emails or calls a backend endpoint) and implement it before submission. Verify the current store wording before submitting.
  • [ ] Age rating questionnaire answered (user-generated content, no ads, no purchases).
  • [ ] User-generated content safeguards satisfy store review: report, block or escalate path, and a way to contact the developer. Reporting exists, confirm the review notes say where.

docs.title: 3.6 Product and policy decisions
docs.text:
• [ ] Push notifications are out of scope for the first release (in-app only). Confirm.
  • [ ] Official badges: the config supports a comma-separated list of ids.
  • [ ] Staff tools intentionally open the web app in the system browser and never share the session.
  • [ ] Admin and moderation dashboards remain web-only.
  • [x] NavigationContainer linking config exists (academiaatlas:// scheme, paths mirror the web routes).
  • [ ] Universal and app links for the https URL: Android intent filters with autoVerify in app.json plus /.well-known/assetlinks.json (needs the Play signing SHA-256), iOS associatedDomains plus apple-app-site-association, all on the final domain.
  • [ ] First launch with no network behaves sensibly.

docs.title: 3.7 Accessibility and quality
docs.text:
• [ ] iOS Dynamic Type and Android font scaling tested.
  • [ ] VoiceOver and TalkBack on the main flows.
  • [ ] Every icon-only button has an accessibility label.
  • [ ] Focus order in the sign-in sheet, filter sheet, report sheet and comments sheet.
  • [ ] Light, dark and system theme changes.
  • [ ] Offline banner, retry and pull to refresh.
  • [ ] Long names and titles, empty states, and 400 field errors.
  • [ ] A small Android phone and a large iPhone.
  • [ ] Keyboard never hides the answer composer, ask form or any sheet input (device test).
  • [ ] No em dash characters ship in copy.

docs.title: 3.8 Store submission
docs.text:
• [ ] App Store Connect and Google Play app records created.
  • [ ] Demo account and review notes provided if the store asks.
  • [ ] Production build uploaded and passed internal testing.
  • [ ] Phased release, then monitor crash-free sessions and API errors.
  • [ ] Previous build kept available for rollback. Release tagged in git, build number in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: 3.9 Release-day smoke test
docs.text:
cd mobile
npm run typecheck
npx expo-doctor
npm run export:web

On a physical device with the production build: - [ ] Install, sign in with Google, browse as a guest, sign out. - [ ] Ask a question and delete it. Answer, vote, comment, mark best answer. - [ ] Open a notification with a link and one without. - [ ] Report content and escalate as a staff account. Lock and unlock a question as staff. - [ ] Open moderation and admin links in the system browser. - [ ] My reports, pages and profile tabs. Dark mode and offline copy. - [ ] Share a question and open the shared link.

docs.title: 3.10 Owner sign-off
docs.text:
• [ ] Backend production URL and CORS confirmed.
  • [ ] Google OAuth production clients confirmed.
  • [ ] Test accounts removed or rotated, dev mode disabled.
  • [ ] Store listings, screenshots and legal pages approved.
  • [ ] Release build uploaded and smoke tested.

docs.title: 4. Cross-surface regression
docs.text:
• [ ] Run the full regression checklist in TESTING.md against production: backend, web and mobile, with all three roles (guest, regular user, staff, admin).
  • [ ] One end-to-end story: sign in on mobile, ask a question, answer it from web as another user, receive the notification on mobile and the email, mark best from mobile, see SOLVED on web.

docs.title: 5. Shared operations
docs.text:
• [ ] Error alerting for backend, web and mobile, and everyone knows where the logs are.
  • [ ] Database backups configured and a restore tested.
  • [ ] Email delivery limits understood, bounce and spam complaints visible.
  • [ ] Production secrets rotated once before launch and stored in the password manager.
  • [ ] Uptime monitoring on /api/v1/health/ with a phone alert.
  • [ ] Rollback procedures tested before launch: Vercel "Promote previous deployment" (both projects) on a preview, previous mobile build kept in the stores.
  • [ ] Support inbox has an owner and a response routine. Abuse reporting has an owner (admins review reports regularly).

docs.title: 6. Launch runbook
docs.text:
1. Freeze changes. Tag the release in git.
  2. Deploy the backend. Run section 1.7 smoke tests and 1.8 permission checks.
  3. Deploy the frontend. Verify sign in, core pages and the production API connection.
  4. Submit or release the mobile build. Verify sign in and core flows on a device.
  5. Run section 4, the cross-surface regression and the end-to-end story.
  6. Announce to the first moderators and representatives, then to students.
  7. If a smoke check fails, stop the rollout and roll back only the affected surface with its tested procedure.

docs.title: 7. First 72 hours
docs.text:
• [ ] Watch error alerts, 5xx rate, 429 rate (too many may mean limits are too tight) and email bounces.
  • [ ] Check the unanswered queue daily and answer or escalate.
  • [ ] Review the first reports and suspensions for tone and consistency.
  • [ ] Collect feedback in one place and triage into the Feature List backlogs.
  • [ ] Decide hotfix versus next release for anything found. Hotfix path: branch from main, pull request, merge, verify on production.

docs.title: 8. Rollback matrix
docs.text: Surface Rollback Notes Backend Redeploy the previous Vercel deployment Check migrations: a backwards-incompatible migration needs a manual plan before launch Web Vercel "Promote previous deployment" Instant, no data change Mobile Halt the phased release, keep the previous build available, EAS Update rollback if used A bad native build cannot be recalled from user devices, which is why the phased release matters

docs.title: Maintainer Playbook (Internal)
docs.text: This is for Mr Nova (project maintainer), not contributors. It's the operating rhythm that keeps Academia Atlas's collaboration running without needing a fresh decision every time something routine comes up. Revisit and adjust this as the project grows, it's a starting point, not a fixed rulebook.

docs.title: The weekly rhythm
docs.text:
Pick one recurring slot, 30 to 45 minutes, same time each week if possible. Contributors will eventually learn to expect activity around that time, which is more valuable than being reachable constantly.

During that slot: 1. Triage new issues, apply labels, move anything genuinely ready into the Ready project board column. 2. Check the Task Board group for stale claims (see below). 3. Review any open pull requests waiting on you. 4. If develop has accumulated a few confirmed-working merges, merge it into main (this is the actual production release). 5. If the Ready column is getting thin, spend 10 minutes grooming docs/contributor-backlog.md and promote one or two more items. 6. Update CONTRIBUTORS.md with anyone whose work merged this week, one line per person is enough. Do this in the same sitting as the recap post below, they're the same mental step, no separate ritual needed. 7. Post a short recap in Announcements (see template below).

You do not need to be responsive outside this slot. Setting that expectation early, gently, protects you from burnout and is completely normal for open source maintainers.

docs.title: Triaging a contributor-opened issue
docs.text: When someone opens an issue themselves (rather than you posting one from contributor-backlog.md): 1. Confirm it's real and reproducible, or ask a clarifying question on the issue if it isn't clear yet. 2. Apply labels (bug/enhancement, plus frontend/backend, plus either good-first-issue or needs-decision). 3. If it needs a design or scope decision from you first, leave it labeled needs-decision and don't let it get claimed yet, note in a comment what you're waiting to decide. 4. Once it's genuinely ready, either let it sit in Ready for anyone to claim, or post it directly in the Task Board group yourself if you want it picked up quickly (useful if the person who reported it wants to fix it themselves and is waiting).

docs.title: Assigning a claimed issue
docs.text:
This is the step that turns a WhatsApp "claiming" reply into a real, trackable claim: 1. When someone comments "I'd like to work on this" on an issue (after claiming it in Task Board), open the issue and add them as the Assignee (right sidebar, "Assignees"). 2. If two people comment on the same issue, the first one to comment gets it, reply on the issue to confirm and let the other person know it's taken (and point them at what else is open, so they don't just leave). 3. That's it, the project board should move it to In Progress automatically once assigned, if you set up that workflow automation in Step 2.

Since contributors work from forks (not direct branches on the main repo), their pull requests will show up as "from fork" when they open one, that's expected, not a configuration problem.

docs.title: Handling stale claims
docs.text: If someone claims a task and goes quiet: - After about 5 to 7 days with no update, reply on the task thread with a friendly check-in ("hey, still working on this one, or should we open it back up?"). People get busy, this isn't an accusation. - No response after another few days: release the task back to the pool, reply "opening this back up for anyone else" and remove their claim. - Never let a task sit claimed-but-dead for weeks, it quietly discourages everyone else from touching it and shrinks your available pool for no reason.

docs.title: Reviewing pull requests
docs.text:
You're new to this too, so a simple standard: does it do what the issue asked, does it match the relevant doc (api-contract.md, design-guide.md, etc.), does it look like it was actually tested. That's enough of a bar for small, well-scoped tasks.

When leaving feedback: - Be specific and kind. "This works, but can you move this logic into the existing helper function instead of duplicating it?" lands much better than "this isn't right." - If it's basically fine with one small issue, approve with a comment asking for the fix, don't block the whole PR over something minor, that's discouraging for a new contributor and slows everything down. - If it's genuinely off track, say so plainly but constructively, and offer a pointer toward the right direction, not just "no." - It's fine to just fix a tiny thing yourself after merging rather than bouncing a PR back and forth over something trivial like a typo.

docs.title: Keeping people engaged
docs.text:
• Public credit, every time. When a PR merges, say so in Announcements with the contributor's name and what they fixed, even if it's small. This costs you thirty seconds and is the single highest-leverage thing you can do for retention.
  • Never let the Ready column run dry. If someone finishes a task and there's nothing else ready to claim, they drift away. Groom the backlog before it becomes urgent, not after someone asks "is there anything else to do?"
  • Vary task difficulty on purpose. Once someone's done two or three good-first-issue tasks, start offering them something intermediate, people stay engaged when they can feel themselves leveling up.
  • A small monthly recap. Even a short post ("this month: 6 tasks closed, welcome to 2 new contributors, here's what's next") makes people feel like they're part of something moving forward, not just doing scattered favors.

docs.title: Weekly recap template (for Announcements)
docs.text:
Week recap 🛠️
✅ Merged: [task names, credit the contributor]
🚧 In progress: [task names, who's on them]
🆕 New tasks up in Task Board: [names]
Thanks everyone, great week.

docs.title: Promoting develop to main (the actual release)
docs.text:
develop accumulates merged PRs continuously. main only changes when you deliberately decide a batch of develop changes is ready to go live, that decision is yours, not automatic, and not tied to any fixed schedule.

Signs it's a good time to promote: - A handful of PRs have merged into develop (there's no magic number, think in terms of "a meaningful, coherent batch," not "every single merge"). - You've clicked through the develop Vercel preview yourself and the merged changes work individually and together, no visual regressions, no broken flows. - Nothing currently in develop is a half-finished or experimental change you're not ready to ship (this shouldn't happen if PRs stay small and scoped, but double-check). - There's no open, known bug in develop that you'd be knowingly shipping.

Don't wait for a large batch out of a sense that releases should be substantial, small, frequent releases are healthier than big infrequent ones, they make it obvious which release introduced a problem if one shows up.

How to actually do it: 1. Open a pull request on GitHub, base main, compare develop. 2. Review the diff yourself, this is your natural checkpoint to see everything that changed since the last release in one place. 3. Merge it. Branch protection means this goes through the same squash-merge button as every other PR, that's fine, a single squash commit on main summarizing "release: profile mobile fix, sidebar separator, loading bar" is a clean, readable release history, exactly what you want main's commit log to look like over time. 4. Merging triggers the live Vercel production deployment automatically, since Production Branch is set to main. 5. Optional, not required: tag it (git tag v0.2.0 && git push origin v0.2.0) if you want a marker to refer back to later. Skip this entirely if it feels like unnecessary ceremony at this stage, it adds no functional value on its own.

After merging, develop and main are back in sync, keep accepting new PRs into develop as normal.

docs.title: When to bring in a co-maintainer
docs.text: Consider giving someone merge rights (not just contributor status) once they've had multiple PRs merged cleanly, shown good judgment in how they communicate, and you'd trust their review of someone else's PR. This isn't urgent, but as the task volume grows, reviewing everything yourself forever doesn't scale. When you get there, GOVERNANCE.md already leaves room for this, it just needs you to update it with the specifics when it happens.

docs.title: When to move to Google Chat
docs.text: You already know the reasoning from earlier. Practical signal for when it's worth the switch: when WhatsApp's lack of threading starts actually costing you time, multiple simultaneous tasks getting confused, hard to find old context, that's the moment, not a fixed date. Until then, WhatsApp is doing its job.

docs.title: Things that don't need a decision every time
docs.text: A few standing defaults, so you don't have to reason from scratch each time: - Bug reports from real users always outrank new feature requests in triage. - If a proposed change isn't in feature-list.md or contributor-backlog.md and isn't a bug, default answer is "let's discuss it in an issue first," not an immediate yes or no. - Anything touching api-contract.md or database-schema.md's documented shape needs your sign-off before work starts, no exceptions, even for a trusted contributor, since it's a contract the frontend depends on. - Small, purely cosmetic PRs (typo fixes, minor copy changes) don't need the full weekly review cycle, merge those whenever you see them.

docs.title: If something feels off
docs.text: Trust that instinct. Most collaboration problems (someone dominating discussion, a PR that feels like scope creep, a tone that's drifting unkind) are much easier to address early and gently than after they've become a pattern. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md exists so you have something concrete to point to if a conversation ever needs it, most of the time a quiet direct message solves it before it needs to go there.

docs.title: Project rename: external follow-up
docs.text:
The in-repository Academia Atlas rename pass is complete. Remaining actions require access to hosting, identity-provider, repository, or release settings:

  • Rename brandnova/academia to brandnova/academia-atlas; update its description, topics, social preview, and avatar.
  • Set the Vercel web project's Root Directory to web. Confirm the backend project's Root Directory remains backend.
  • Update the Google Cloud OAuth consent-screen name and logo. Change authorized origins only if the product domain changes.
  • After renaming the repository, verify GitHub Pages and publish MkDocs at https://brandnova.github.io/academia-atlas/.
  • Update local origin and fork upstream remotes after the GitHub rename.
  • Check PythonAnywhere WSGI, source paths, and scheduled jobs for old checkout paths; update only if any are present.
  • After merge, promote develop to main and verify web, API, docs, and mobile build configurations. Tag the release if desired.

The task checklist is maintained in gitignore/Next.md.

docs.title: Quick Workflow
docs.text: This is the short version of CONTRIBUTING.md, the exact steps for going from "I want to help" to "my change is live." Keep this open in a tab the first few times, it'll be second nature after that.

docs.title: Found a bug on your own, before you even get to step 1?
docs.text:
Search the repo's Issues tab first to check it isn't already reported. If it's new, open one using the Bug Report template, be specific (exact page, what you expected, what happened), then drop a one-line mention in General with the link. A maintainer will triage it before it's ready to claim.

Security issue instead of a regular bug? Don't post it anywhere public, see SECURITY.md.

docs.title: 1. Claim a task
docs.text: Tasks are posted in the WhatsApp Task Board group, one per message, each linking to a GitHub issue. Reply "claiming" on the task's message before you start. This avoids two people working on the same thing.

docs.title: 2. Confirm the claim on GitHub
docs.text: Replying in WhatsApp isn't the official claim, GitHub is. Open the linked issue and comment "I'd like to work on this." Wait until a maintainer adds you as the Assignee (you'll get a GitHub notification), that's your actual green light to start. If nobody's assigned it within a day or so, a friendly nudge on the issue is fine.

docs.title: 3. Fork and get the code
docs.text:
You work from your own fork, not the main repo directly, that's the normal model here (see CONTRIBUTING.md's "Fork, clone, and branch" for the full explanation of why).

  1. Click "Fork" on the GitHub repo page.
  2. Clone your fork: bash git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/academia-atlas.git cd academia-atlas git remote add upstream https://github.com/brandnova/academia-atlas.git
  3. Sync and branch: bash git checkout develop git fetch upstream git merge upstream/develop git checkout -b fix/short-description

Use fix/... for bug fixes, feat/... for small features. Match the name to what the issue is about, for example fix/profile-mobile-layout.

docs.title: 4. Set up locally
docs.text: See README.md's "Getting Started" section for backend and web setup, it has the exact commands. Ask in General if anything doesn't work, environment setup problems are extremely common and not a reflection on you.

docs.title: 5. Make your change
docs.text: Keep it scoped to exactly what the issue describes. Notice something else that's broken while you're in there? Great, that's a new issue, not something to fix in the same PR.

docs.title: 6. Commit and push to your fork
docs.text:
git add .
git commit -m "fix: short description of what changed"
git push -u origin fix/short-description

fix: for bug fixes, feat: for features, docs: for documentation changes.

docs.title: 7. Open the pull request
docs.text:
On GitHub, open a PR from your fork's branch into brandnova/academia-atlas's develop branch (not main), you'll see a "compare across forks" option when you start a new PR from your fork. Fill out the template, most importantly: - Closes #<issue number> so it links back automatically - A screenshot if it's a visual change - How you tested it

Then post the PR link back in the Task Board group, reply on your original claim message so it's easy to find.

docs.title: 8. Review
docs.text: Nova (or another maintainer) reviews it. Expect comments and requested changes, completely normal, not a sign you did something wrong. Push more commits to the same branch to address feedback, they'll show up on the same PR automatically. If it sits a while and develop moves on, sync your branch with git fetch upstream and git merge upstream/develop before asking for another look.

docs.title: 9. Merge
docs.text: Once approved, it gets squash-merged into develop. You'll see it move to Done on the project board, and a batch of develop changes gets released to production periodically. You're now a credited Academia Atlas contributor, visible on the GitHub contributor graph and in the project's recognition materials.

docs.title: If you get stuck
docs.text: Ask in General before spending more than 20 to 30 minutes stuck on something environmental (setup, tooling, git). Questions there help the next person too, so there's no such thing as a bad question.

docs.title: Academia Atlas Regression Testing
docs.text: Use this checklist for regression checks across the backend, web and mobile client. Release-only and provider-account setup is tracked separately in DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
Run the backend test suite from the backend directory:

cd backend
make test

Confirm /api/v1/health/ responds and exercise the documented authentication, permission, question-and-answer, search, report and notification flows against the API contract. Verify both allowed and denied role actions; the backend is the authority for permissions.

docs.title: Web
docs.text:
Run the web checks from the web directory:

cd web
npm run check
npm run build

Manually check guest browsing, Google sign-in and session refresh; question and answer creation, editing and voting; comments, notifications and reports; and moderator, representative and admin actions. Verify loading, empty, error and populated states, plus light and dark themes and narrow-screen layouts.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
cd backend && make run-lan          # 0.0.0.0:8000 for a phone on Wi-Fi, or run the default server and use adb reverse
cd mobile && cp .env.example .env && npm install && npx expo start -c

Alternatives to the LAN server: adb reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000 with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000/api/v1, or a deployed https backend. The backend .env must allow your LAN IP in DJANGO_DEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS and the Expo web origin in CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (http://localhost:8081). Health check: curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/health/.

docs.title: Test users without Google
docs.text:
cd backend && python manage.py seed_demo_data && python manage.py print_test_tokens

One hour tokens for test-admin@example.com (admin), test-staff@example.com (moderator and representative for UNILAG) and test-user@example.com. In development builds set EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_MODE=1 and use Developer access on Login or in the sign-in sheet, paste both tokens. It does not exist in preview or production builds.

docs.title: Login and session
docs.text:
1. First launch: headline, Google button, Browse as guest. Guest browsing needs no account, Alerts and Profile show sign-in states.
  2. Google (installed build): the native account chooser opens, cancelling shows nothing, a wrong or missing setup shows a clear message, Log out then sign in shows the chooser again. Expo Go explains that it needs the installed build.
  3. Suspended account (403) shows the backend message and the support contact. Invalid token (401) shows "We couldn't verify your Google account. Please try again."
  4. Backend down at startup with a stored session: stays signed in on the cached user, recovers when the server returns. Guests never see an expired-session sheet. An invalid refresh token clears the session and shows the expired sheet.

docs.title: Home, Search, Schools, Tags
docs.text:
1. Home: search pill, school card strip (tile, live question count, names, location), popular tags, recent questions. Pull to refresh updates all of it, View more appends without duplicates.
  2. Search: "Searching..." then results after about 500 ms, count line, tag filter (chip with x, More tags sheet with search), scrolling closes the keyboard.
  3. Schools: name search, filter sheet (Has hub, type, ownership, state) with a badge count, Clear all, empty result offers Clear filters.
  4. School page: hero, Ask prefilled, status and department chips, Sort sheet, View more. No hub shows the request card and the request sheet.
  5. Tags: Popular or A to Z, search, View more. Tag questions: status chips.

docs.title: Question, answers, comments
docs.text:
1. Header: status, title, asked by with badge, school link, department, views, tags, Markdown body (headings are plain text).
  2. Follow toggles, guests get the sign-in sheet. Staff see Lock and Unlock only for their hub, and it works repeatedly, also after reopening the question.
  3. Best answer pin, View in list scrolls and flashes the answer. A deep link with an answer id does the same.
  4. Answers: byline above the body, vote up, down, remove, switching works and a failure never leaves a wrong count, Mark as best for the question author only.
  5. Kebab sheets: own content Edit and Delete, others Report, staff also Escalate. Question also has Share link (title, status, counts, URL).
  6. Locked question hides the composer. Guests see "Sign in to answer this question". The composer and its toolbar stay above the keyboard.
  7. Comments sheet: list, add, View more over 20, count on the answer updates, own Edit and Delete, others Report, staff Escalate, everything stays inside the one sheet and Back steps back first.

docs.title: Ask and edit
docs.text:
1. School step lists only schools with active hubs. Form step shows "Posting to ...", field errors appear under their field.
  2. Tags: popular list on focus, live search after about 300 ms, free text, chips removable, 50 character limit message.
  3. Editor: toggles formatting off, continues lists, wraps links, preview matches display, long text scrolls inside the editor.
  4. The form and Post question stay above the keyboard. Edit loads fresh every time, also after saving once, with loading and error states.

docs.title: Notifications, Profile, Reports, Pages
docs.text:
1. Notifications: All and Unread, unread rows are tinted with a dot, tapping marks read, rows with a link open the question at the answer, rows without one only mark read, Mark all read, admin-only types show Open on web. The list refetches on tab focus.
  2. Profile: card with stats, Edit name (trimmed, blank blocked, backend error under the field), four tabs each paged with View more, staff see the web buttons, My reports, Policies, theme, Log out.
  3. My reports: explains privacy, filters, status labels, Content removed has no View link, never shows reviewer or escalation data.
  4. Pages: staff and draft labels for the roles that get them, pull to refresh, headings render on pages.
  5. Report and escalate: a reason is required, escalate is one button, "already reported" shows the friendly message. Staff web handoff shows a confirmation sheet with the URL and opens the system browser with no token.

docs.title: Global checks
docs.text:
• Loading, empty, error with Retry, "Can't connect" for network failures, offline banner, pull to refresh.
  • Dark mode by system and manual, no flash, text uses ink and muted tokens, a theme change keeps working across screens.
  • 429, 502, 503, 504 and no-network copy matches the contract. 400 errors attach to fields.
  • Drawer closes on backdrop, Back and swipe. Tab bar matches the mockup. Wordmark stays on one line.
  • Deep links from a closed and a running app: academiaatlas://questions/{id}, with #answer-{id}, schools/{id}/{slug}, tags/{tag}.
  • Reduced motion stops the skeleton pulse. The largest system font keeps tab bar, chips, rows and sheets usable. TalkBack reads every control and announces form errors.
  • Error boundary fallback appears on a render crash and Try again recovers.
  • No moderation or admin screens in navigation. Touch targets at least 44pt. No em dash characters in source or copy.
  • Preview and production builds have no developer sheet and no seeded tokens.

docs.title: Automated checks
docs.text:
cd mobile
npm run typecheck
npx expo-doctor
npm run export:web
npx expo export --platform android --output-dir /tmp/atlas-export

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: All endpoints below are namespaced under /api/v1/. For example, GET /api/schools/ in this document means GET /api/v1/schools/. Breaking changes will ship under a new version prefix (/api/v2/); /api/v1/ will be maintained for a documented deprecation window once a v2 exists.

docs.title: Authentication Modes
docs.text:
• User auth - JWT bearer token, obtained via the Google login flow below. Used by the frontend and any user-driven action.
  • API client auth (Future) - X-API-Key header, used by registered third-party consumers hitting public read-only endpoints. Not available in MVP.

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/health/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "academia-backend",
  "checks": {
    "database": "ok",
    "cache": "ok"
  },
  "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

No authentication required. status is "degraded" if the database is unreachable, a cache outage alone does not count as degraded, caching is designed to fail open (see project-plan.md). Useful for uptime monitoring and load balancer health checks, not intended for frontend application logic.

docs.title: How Google Auth Works (Frontend Implementation Guide)
docs.text:
This backend does not use Django's full server-side social-auth flow. Instead, the frontend obtains a Google access token directly using Google Identity Services, then hands that token to our backend, which verifies it by calling Google's own userinfo endpoint. This means: no client secret on the backend, no redirect-based OAuth dance, and a small, predictable request/response contract.

One-time setup (Google Cloud Console): 1. Create a project (or use an existing one) at console.cloud.google.com. 2. Configure the OAuth consent screen (External, testing or published as needed). 3. Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID of type Web application. 4. Add your frontend's origin(s) under Authorized JavaScript origins (e.g. http://localhost:3000, and your production domain later). 5. You only need the Client ID on the frontend, no client secret is used anywhere in this flow.

Frontend flow, step by step: 1. Load Google's Identity Services script: <script src="https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client" async defer></script> 2. Initialize a token client with your Client ID and the scopes email profile:

   const client = google.accounts.oauth2.initTokenClient({
     client_id: "YOUR_CLIENT_ID.apps.googleusercontent.com",
     scope: "email profile",
     callback: (tokenResponse) => {
       // tokenResponse.access_token is what you send to our backend
     },
   });
  1. On your "Sign in with Google" button click, call client.requestAccessToken(). This opens Google's consent popup and returns an access_token in the callback.
  2. POST that token to our backend: POST /api/v1/auth/google/ with body { "access_token": "<token_from_step_3>" }.
  3. Our backend verifies the token against Google, creates the user if this is their first login, and returns our own JWT pair (access/refresh) plus the user object, see the endpoint spec below.
  4. Store the JWT pair (httpOnly cookie is preferred once you're past local dev, in-memory/localStorage is fine for early development) and attach Authorization: Bearer <access> to every subsequent authenticated request.
  5. When a request comes back 401 because the access token expired, call POST /api/v1/auth/refresh/ with the stored refresh token to get a new access token, see below. Note refresh tokens rotate on use, so store the new one returned each time.
  6. On logout, POST the current refresh token to /api/v1/auth/logout/ (this blacklists it server-side) and clear locally stored tokens.

This is the entire flow, there's no separate "callback URL" or server-rendered redirect page to build, it's a client-side popup plus one API call.

docs.title: Native clients
docs.text:
Any Google OAuth client that obtains an access token with the email and profile scopes can use this endpoint. The backend verifies the token through Google's userinfo endpoint; the mobile app uses separate OAuth client IDs for each platform.

Login and token refresh are both rate limited to 10 requests per minute per client (see Rate Limits below), to slow down credential-stuffing style abuse.

docs.title: Google Login
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/auth/google/

Request:

{
  "access_token": "google_oauth_access_token"
}

Response (200 OK):

{
  "access": "jwt_access_token",
  "refresh": "jwt_refresh_token",
  "user": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "full_name": "John Doe",
    "avatar": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/...",
    "is_admin": false,
    "moderator_for": [
      {
        "hub_id": "uuid",
        "school": { "id": "uuid", "name": "University of Lagos", "slug": "unilag" }
      }
    ],
    "representative_for": [
      {
        "hub_id": "uuid",
        "school": { "id": "uuid", "name": "University of Lagos", "slug": "unilag" }
      }
    ],
    "stats": {
      "question_count": 12,
      "answer_count": 34,
      "best_answer_count": 9,
      "comment_count": 21
    }
  }
}

Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "access_token is required"
}

Response (401 Unauthorized):

{
  "error": "Invalid Google token"
}

Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "error": "Your account has been suspended"
}

Behavior notes: first login for an email creates the User record automatically (no separate signup step); subsequent logins reuse the same user and refresh full_name/avatar from Google if they've changed. A suspended account (is_active: false) is rejected at login with a 403 and a clear message, rather than issuing a token pair that only fails on the next authenticated request. Google-authenticated accounts also have set_unusable_password() called explicitly at creation, and a Google userinfo response with email_verified: false is rejected the same as an invalid token, closing two hardening gaps ahead of the planned email/ password auth phase.

docs.title: Refresh Token
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/auth/refresh/

Request:

{
  "refresh": "jwt_refresh_token"
}

Response (200 OK):

{
  "access": "new_jwt_access_token",
  "refresh": "new_jwt_refresh_token"
}

Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "refresh": ["This field is required."]
}

Response (401 Unauthorized):

{
  "error": "Token is invalid or expired"
}

Refresh tokens rotate on every use and the previous one is blacklisted, always store whichever refresh token was most recently issued.

docs.title: Logout
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/auth/logout/

Request:

{
  "refresh": "jwt_refresh_token"
}

Response (204 No Content): Empty

Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "refresh token is required"
}

or

{
  "error": "Invalid or already blacklisted token"
}

Response (401 Unauthorized):

{
  "error": "Authentication credentials were not provided."
}

Blacklists the given refresh token server-side, it can no longer be used to obtain new access tokens.

docs.title: Get Current User
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/users/me/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "full_name": "John Doe",
  "avatar": "https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/...",
  "is_admin": false,
  "moderator_for": [
    {
      "hub_id": "uuid",
      "school": { "id": "uuid", "name": "University of Lagos", "slug": "unilag" }
    }
  ],
  "representative_for": [
    {
      "hub_id": "uuid",
      "school": { "id": "uuid", "name": "University of Lagos", "slug": "unilag" }
    }
  ],
  "stats": {
    "question_count": 12,
    "answer_count": 34,
    "best_answer_count": 9,
    "comment_count": 21
  },
  "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

moderator_for and representative_for list every hub (with its school) where this user currently holds an active assignment. Both are empty arrays for a user with no such assignments. stats is a count-only summary for this user's own activity (own question/answer/comment counts, plus how many of their answers are marked best), intended for badge-style display (e.g. "Posts (3)"), the actual objects are fetched via the endpoints below, not embedded here. This same shape, including stats, is also returned in the user field of the Google Login response. See "Frontend Permission Model" below for how to use the role fields. Only hubs that are currently active are listed. A deactivated hub's assignments are kept but hidden here until the hub is reactivated.

docs.title: Update Current User
docs.text:
Endpoint: PATCH /api/v1/users/me/

Request:

{
  "full_name": "Johnathan Doe"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "full_name": ["This field may not be blank."]
}
