A blank, whitespace-only, or null full_name is rejected, as is one longer than the field's maximum length. Omitting full_name leaves the account unchanged and returns 200. The name is stored trimmed.

Response (200 OK): Same as GET /api/v1/users/me/

docs.title: Search Users (Admin or School Representative)
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/users/search/

Query Parameters: - search - Search by email or full_name, required, empty results if omitted

Response (200 OK):

{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "full_name": "Jane Smith",
      "email": "jane@example.com",
      "avatar": "https://..."
    }
  ]
}

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "error": "You do not have permission to search for users"
}

Available to platform admins and to any user with an active SchoolRepresentativeAssignment for at least one hub, not scoped to a specific hub, since the assignment endpoints themselves already enforce hub-specific permission at the point of use. This exists specifically so a School Representative can find a user_id to pass into POST /hubs/{hub_id}/moderators/ without needing admin access. Not paginated, results capped at 10, matching the existing Tags search-as-you-type pattern.

docs.title: Frontend Permission Model
docs.text: The API enforces every permission independently, server-side, on every write. The fields described here exist purely so the frontend can show or hide the right links, buttons, and forms without guessing, they are a UX convenience, not a substitute for backend enforcement, hiding a button never replaces the 403 a user would get if they attempted the action directly.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
• User: any authenticated account. Can ask/answer/comment/vote/report/ request a hub.
  • Moderator: a User with an active entry in that hub's moderator_for. Can additionally see that hub's unanswered-questions queue.
  • School Representative: a User with an active entry in that hub's representative_for. Can additionally manage departments for that hub's school, and assign/remove moderators for that hub.
  • Admin: is_admin: true. Implicitly satisfies every Moderator and Representative check for every hub, in addition to admin-only actions (approve/reject hub activations, manage schools, assign representatives, resolve reports, manage users). An admin's moderator_for/ representative_for arrays are not artificially populated with every hub, is_admin alone is the signal to check for blanket access.

docs.title: How a user gets a role
docs.text:
There is no self-service way to become a Moderator or Representative. An admin assigns both explicitly: - POST /hubs/{hub_id}/representatives/ (admin only) makes a user a Representative for that hub. - POST /hubs/{hub_id}/moderators/ (admin, or an existing Representative for that hub) makes a user a Moderator for that hub.

The newly assigned user does not see this reflected until their next GET /users/me/ call picks up the new moderator_for/representative_for entry. An in-app MODERATOR_ASSIGNED notification now fires for moderator and representative assignments, but it does not update the current-user fields in an already loaded session. Refetch the current user after login and when navigating into a school or hub the person might administer, rather than relying on those fields updating automatically mid-session.

docs.title: Deriving what to show
docs.text:
Given the current user's moderator_for/representative_for/is_admin, and a specific school or hub the person is viewing:

Show this... ...when "Ask a question" any authenticated user "Request hub activation" any authenticated user, on a school with has_hub: false "Manage departments" (create/edit) for a school is_admin is true, OR that school's id appears in representative_for[].school.id "Assign / remove moderators" for a hub is_admin is true, OR that hub's id appears in representative_for[].hub_id "Assign / remove representatives" for a hub is_admin is true only "Unanswered questions" queue link, scoped to a hub is_admin is true, OR that hub's id appears in moderator_for[].hub_id Admin dashboard (schools, activation requests, reports, users) is_admin is true only

Matching against representative_for[].school.id directly (rather than resolving a hub id first) is the fastest way to check department-management access for a school page, since the school's own id is already on hand wherever a school is being displayed.

docs.title: List Schools
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/schools/

Query Parameters: - search - Search by name or short_name - has_hub - Filter schools with/without hub (true/false) - institution_type - Filter by UNIVERSITY/POLYTECHNIC/COLLEGE_OF_EDUCATION - ownership - Filter by FEDERAL/STATE/PRIVATE - state - Filter by Nigerian state (exact match, case-insensitive) - is_active - Admin only, filter by active status (true/false). Ignored for non-admin requests, which are always restricted to active schools regardless of this param - page - Page number (default: 1) - page_size - Items per page (default: 20, max: 100)

Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 100,
  "next": "https://api.academia.com/api/v1/schools/?page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "University of Lagos",
      "short_name": "UNILAG",
      "slug": "unilag",
      "location": "Lagos, Nigeria",
      "website": "https://unilag.edu.ng",
      "has_hub": true,
      "is_active": true,
      "institution_type": "UNIVERSITY",
      "ownership": "FEDERAL",
      "state": "Lagos",
      "country": "Nigeria",
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

Caching & Visibility Behavior: - Cache: Public requests are cached with prefix school-list:query using CACHE_TTL_SHORT (60 seconds). - Admin Bypass: Authenticated Platform Admins bypass the cache completely (to see live entries and inactive/deactivated schools, which are filtered out for regular users/guests). - Invalidation: Wiped automatically on POST school creation or PATCH school updates.

All three new filters combine with AND when used together, and with the existing search/has_hub filters. institution_type and ownership values are case-insensitive on input (uppercased before matching), state matches case-insensitively against the stored value.

docs.title: Get School
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/schools/{school_id}/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "name": "University of Lagos",
  "short_name": "UNILAG",
  "slug": "unilag",
  "location": "Lagos, Nigeria",
  "website": "https://unilag.edu.ng",
  "has_hub": true,
  "is_active": true,
  "verification_status": "VERIFIED",
  "institution_type": "UNIVERSITY",
  "ownership": "FEDERAL",
  "state": "Lagos",
  "country": "Nigeria",
  "regulatory_code": null,
  "source_url": null,
  "last_verified_at": null,
  "departments": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "Computer Science",
      "code": "CSC",
      "question_count": 42,
      "is_active": true
    }
  ],
  "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "School not found"
}

Caching & Visibility Behavior: - Cache: Public detail views are cached as school-detail:{school_id} using CACHE_TTL_MEDIUM (300 seconds). - Admin Bypass: Authenticated Platform Admins bypass this cache entirely and view live data (including inactive status). - Invalidation: Cleared on PATCH school update of the school, or POST/PATCH operations on the school's departments.

regulatory_code, source_url, and last_verified_at are null for every school until the NUC/NBTE/NCCE directory import lands and/or an admin sets them manually. institution_type, ownership, and state are also nullable, expect null on any school created before that import.

docs.title: Get School by Slug
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/schools/by-slug/{slug}/

Response (200 OK): Same as GET /api/v1/schools/{school_id}/

Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "School not found"
}

Caching Behavior: - Cache: Non-admin responses are cached as school-by-slug:{slug} using CACHE_TTL_MEDIUM (300 seconds). Platform admins bypass the cache and can retrieve inactive schools.

This is an additive lookup path alongside the existing UUID-based one, both remain valid indefinitely. slug is generated once at creation from short_name and never regenerated, so a bookmarked or shared URL never breaks even if short_name changes later.

docs.title: Create School (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/schools/

Request:

{
  "name": "University of Ibadan",
  "short_name": "UI",
  "location": "Ibadan, Nigeria",
  "website": "https://ui.edu.ng",
  "institution_type": "UNIVERSITY",
  "ownership": "FEDERAL",
  "state": "Oyo",
  "country": "Nigeria",
  "regulatory_code": null,
  "source_url": null,
  "last_verified_at": null
}

short_name is automatically uppercased on save. location, website, and every field from institution_type through last_verified_at are optional. A slug is auto-generated from short_name (e.g. "UI" → "ui") and is never regenerated. country defaults to "Nigeria" if omitted.

Response (201 Created): Same as GET /api/v1/schools/{school_id}/

Error Responses:

// 400 Bad Request - Duplicate school name or short_name
{
  "name": ["school with this name already exists."],
  "short_name": ["school with this short name already exists."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - Duplicate regulatory_code
{
  "regulatory_code": ["school with this regulatory code already exists."]
}

Invalidation Note: Invalidates and clears all entries matching the school-list cache prefix.

docs.title: Update School (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: PATCH /api/v1/schools/{school_id}/

Request: Same fields as POST (see Create School above), all optional. Accepts "is_active": true/false. This is also how regulatory_code, source_url, and last_verified_at get set or corrected after the fact, whether by the import process or by an admin.

Response (200 OK): Same as GET /api/v1/schools/{school_id}/

Invalidation Note: Invalidates school-detail:{school_id} cache key and the school-list cache prefix.

docs.title: Delete School (Admin Only)
docs.text: There is no dedicated DELETE endpoint. "Deleting" a school is a soft-delete, send PATCH /api/v1/schools/{school_id}/ with {"is_active": false}. This keeps foreign-key relationships (hubs, questions, etc.) intact rather than orphaning them, and is easily reversible. A deactivated school is excluded from list/detail responses for non-admins.

docs.title: Get Hub
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/hubs/{hub_id}/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "school": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "name": "University of Lagos",
    "short_name": "UNILAG",
    "slug": "unilag",
    "location": "Lagos, Nigeria"
  },
  "is_active": true,
  "activated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "departments": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "Computer Science",
      "code": "CSC",
      "question_count": 42
    }
  ],
  "question_count": 150,
  "moderator_count": 3
}

Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "Hub not found"
}

Caching & Visibility Behavior: - Cache: Cached as hub-detail:{hub_id} using CACHE_TTL_SHORT (60 seconds). - Inactive hubs: A deactivated hub returns 404 to everyone except platform admins. Admins bypass the cache entirely and can read an inactive hub (is_active: false), so it can be found and reactivated. - Invalidation: Cleared automatically on: - Approve Activation Request (hub activation). - Update Hub (deactivate or reactivate). - Assign / Remove Moderator.

docs.title: Get Hub by School
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/hubs/by-school/{school_id}/

Response (200 OK): Same as GET /api/v1/hubs/{hub_id}/

Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "Hub not found for this school"
}

Caching & Visibility Behavior: - Cache: Cached as hub-by-school:{school_id} using CACHE_TTL_SHORT (60 seconds). - Inactive hubs: A deactivated hub returns 404 to everyone except platform admins. Admins bypass the cache entirely and can read an inactive hub (is_active: false), so it can be found and reactivated. - Invalidation: Cleared automatically on: - Approve Activation Request (hub activation). - Update Hub (deactivate or reactivate). - Assign / Remove Moderator.

docs.title: Get Hub by Slug
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/hubs/by-slug/{slug}/

Response (200 OK): Same as GET /api/v1/hubs/{hub_id}/

Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "Hub not found for this school"
}

Caching & Visibility Behavior: - Cache: Cached as hub-by-slug:{slug} using CACHE_TTL_SHORT (60 seconds). - Inactive hubs: A deactivated hub returns 404 to everyone except platform admins. Admins bypass the cache entirely and can read an inactive hub (is_active: false), so it can be found and reactivated. - Invalidation: Cleared automatically on: - Approve Activation Request (hub activation). - Update Hub (deactivate or reactivate). - Assign / Remove Moderator.

docs.title: Update Hub (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: PATCH /api/v1/hubs/{hub_id}/

Takes a hub offline or brings it back. This is the only editable field.

Request:

{
  "is_active": false
}

Response (200 OK): Same as GET /api/v1/hubs/{hub_id}/

Error Responses:

// 400 Bad Request - missing or non-boolean is_active
{
  "is_active": ["This field is required."]
}

// 403 Forbidden - not an admin (representatives cannot do this)
{
  "error": "You do not have permission to perform this action"
}

// 404 Not Found
{
  "error": "Hub not found"
}

A deactivated hub behaves like a soft-delete: it returns 404 to non-admins on every hub route, its school's has_hub becomes false, and no new questions can be asked in it. Existing questions, answers, and comments are kept and remain readable. Moderator and representative assignments are kept untouched, so reactivating restores the team, but the hub disappears from the moderator_for and representative_for lists on GET /users/me/ while it is offline, and the moderator and representative management endpoints return 404 until it is reactivated. Repeating the current state returns 200 and changes nothing. A genuine change is recorded in the admin action log (HUB_DEACTIVATED / HUB_REACTIVATED) and invalidates the hub and school caches.

docs.title: Request Hub Activation
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/hubs/activation-requests/

Request:

{
  "school_id": "uuid",
  "notes": "Our university needs a hub for students"
}

Response (201 Created):

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "school": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "name": "University of Lagos",
    "short_name": "UNILAG",
    "slug": "unilag",
    "location": "Lagos, Nigeria"
  },
  "user": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "full_name": "John Doe"
  },
  "status": "PENDING",
  "notes": "Our university needs a hub for students",
  "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

Error Responses:

// 400 Bad Request - School already has an active hub
{
  "school_id": ["This school already has an active hub."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - A pending request already exists for this school
{
  "school_id": ["There is already a pending activation request for this school."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - School doesn't exist
{
  "school_id": ["School not found."]
}

A new request is blocked if the target school already has an active hub, or if a PENDING request for that school already exists, this prevents duplicate/spam requests from piling up before an admin reviews the first one.

Submitting a request sends every active admin a NEW_ACTIVATION_REQUEST notification, in-app only, excluding the requester if they happen to be an admin. A school whose hub was deactivated can be requested again. Approving that request reactivates the existing hub.

docs.title: List Activation Requests (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/hubs/activation-requests/

Query Parameters: - status - PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED - page - Page number

Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 5,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "school": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "name": "University of Lagos",
        "short_name": "UNILAG"
      },
      "user": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "full_name": "John Doe"
      },
      "status": "PENDING",
      "notes": "Our university needs a hub for students",
      "rejection_reason": null,
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Approve Activation Request (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/hubs/activation-requests/{request_id}/approve/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "message": "Hub activated successfully",
  "hub": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "school": {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "University of Lagos",
      "short_name": "UNILAG"
    },
    "activated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "This activation request has already been reviewed"
}

Approving sends the requesting user a HUB_ACTIVATED notification (in-app and email).

Invalidation Note: Automatically invalidates hub-detail:{hub_id}, hub-by-school:{school_id}, hub-by-slug:{slug}, school-detail:{school_id}, and the school-list prefix.

docs.title: Reject Activation Request (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/hubs/activation-requests/{request_id}/reject/

Request:

{
  "reason": "School not verified"
}

Response (200 OK):

{
  "message": "Activation request rejected",
  "status": "REJECTED"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "This activation request has already been reviewed"
}

Rejecting sends the requesting user a HUB_ACTIVATION_REJECTED notification (email and in-app). The reason field is optional text of at most 1000 characters (whitespace-only counts as no reason, a non-string or over-long value returns a 400 field error and leaves the request pending). It is stored as rejection_reason, shown in GET /hubs/activation-requests/, and quoted in the email. rejection_reason is null for approved and pending requests and for rejections made without a reason.

docs.title: List Departments
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/schools/{school_id}/departments/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "Computer Science",
      "code": "CSC",
      "question_count": 42,
      "is_active": true
    }
  ]
}

This endpoint is not paginated. For regular users and guests, only active departments (is_active: true) are returned. Authenticated Platform Admins and School Representatives for this school's hub see all departments, including inactive ones (so they can reactivate them via PATCH).

docs.title: Create Department (School Representative or Admin)
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/schools/{school_id}/departments/

Request:

{
  "name": "Data Science",
  "code": "DSC"
}

code is optional (can be omitted or sent as null). name is required and is case-sensitively unique per school (enforced at the database level).

Response (201 Created): Same as department object in List Departments above

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "name": ["A department with this name already exists for this school."]
}

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "error": "You do not have permission to perform this action"
}

Requires an active SchoolRepresentativeAssignment for this school's hub, or platform admin status.

Invalidation Note: Creating a department invalidates the school-detail:{school_id} cache key of its parent school.

docs.title: Update Department (School Representative or Admin)
docs.text:
Endpoint: PATCH /api/v1/departments/{department_id}/

Request:

{
  "name": "Computer Science and Engineering",
  "code": "CSE",
  "is_active": false
}

All fields are optional (partial PATCH). Sending "is_active": false is the soft-delete path; setting it back to true reactivates the department.

Response (200 OK): Same as department object

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "error": "You do not have permission to perform this action"
}

Same permission requirement as Create Department above.

Invalidation Note: Updating a department invalidates the school-detail:{school_id} cache key for its corresponding parent school.

docs.title: List Questions
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/questions/

Query Parameters: - hub - Filter by hub ID - department - Filter by department ID - status - OPEN/ANSWERED/SOLVED - tag - Filter by tag name - author - Filter by author user ID - search - Search in title and body - ordering - created_at/-created_at/views/-views - page - Page number - page_size - Items per page (default: 20, max: 50)

Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 150,
  "next": "https://api.academia.com/api/v1/questions/?page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "title": "How do I calculate my CGPA?",
      "slug": "how-do-i-calculate-my-cgpa",
      "body": "I'm confused about the grading system...",
      "status": "SOLVED",
      "view_count": 120,
      "is_locked": false,
      "author": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "full_name": "John Doe",
        "avatar": "https://..."
      },
      "hub": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "school": {
          "name": "University of Lagos",
          "short_name": "UNILAG",
          "slug": "unilag"
        }
      },
      "department": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "name": "Computer Science"
      },
      "tags": ["gpa", "grading", "calculation"],
      "answer_count": 3,
      "best_answer_id": "uuid",
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Create Question
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/questions/

Rate limited to 30 requests per hour per user (see Rate Limits below).

Request:

{
  "title": "How do I calculate my CGPA?",
  "body": "I'm confused about the grading system at UNILAG...",
  "hub_id": "uuid",
  "department_id": "uuid",
  "tags": ["gpa", "grading", "calculation"]
}

Response (201 Created): Same as GET /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/

Error Responses:

// 400 Bad Request - Missing required fields
{
  "title": ["This field is required."],
  "body": ["This field is required."],
  "hub_id": ["This field is required."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - Hub doesn't have this department
{
  "department_id": ["Department does not belong to this hub's school."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - Hub doesn't exist
{
  "hub_id": ["Hub with ID 'uuid' does not exist."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - tag name too long
{
  "tags": ["Tag names must be 50 characters or fewer."]
}

Creating a question sends a NEW_QUESTION notification, in-app only, to every user with an active ModeratorAssignment for that hub, excluding the question's own author.

docs.title: Get Question
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "title": "How do I calculate my CGPA?",
  "slug": "how-do-i-calculate-my-cgpa",
  "body": "I'm confused about the grading system...",
  "status": "SOLVED",
  "view_count": 120,
  "is_locked": false,
  "is_following": false,
  "author": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "full_name": "John Doe",
    "avatar": "https://..."
  },
  "hub": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "school": {
      "name": "University of Lagos",
      "short_name": "UNILAG",
      "slug": "unilag"
    }
  },
  "department": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "name": "Computer Science"
  },
  "tags": ["gpa", "grading", "calculation"],
  "answers": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "body": "To calculate your CGPA...",
      "is_best": true,
      "vote_score": 15,
      "user_vote": "UP",
      "author": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "full_name": "Jane Smith",
        "avatar": "https://..."
      },
      "comment_count": 2,
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "answer_count": 3,
  "best_answer_id": "uuid",
  "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "Question not found"
}

view_count only increments for authenticated requests, anonymous views are never counted. Increments are deduplicated per user for 24 hours (a rolling window, not a calendar-day reset), a signed-in user repeatedly refreshing the same question within that window will not keep inflating the count. This is cache-backed, not a permanent per-user view record, no history of who viewed what is stored anywhere.

is_following reflects only the requesting user's own follow state, always false for anonymous requests, see Follow Question below.

docs.title: Update Question
docs.text:
Endpoint: PATCH /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/

Request:

{
  "title": "Updated title",
  "body": "Updated body",
  "department_id": "uuid",
  "tags": ["gpa", "updated"]
}

Response (200 OK): Same as GET /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "error": "You do not have permission to edit this question"
}

Note: - status is not an editable field on this endpoint. It changes only as a side effect: creating the first answer moves a question from OPEN to ANSWERED, marking a best answer moves it to SOLVED, deleting an answer can move it back to ANSWERED or OPEN depending on what remains (see Delete Answer below). - SOLVED means "this question has a designated best answer," not "this question is closed." New answers can be submitted to a question at any status, including SOLVED, a question is never locked to further input purely because an owner picked a favorite. Adding a plain answer to a SOLVED question does not change its status, only removing the current best answer (or the owner marking a different answer best) affects SOLVED status. - slug on Question is purely cosmetic, meant for building readable URLs like /questions/{id}/{slug}, it is not unique and is not used for lookups. Editing a question's title regenerates its slug.

docs.title: Delete Question
docs.text:
Endpoint: DELETE /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/

Response (204 No Content): Empty

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "error": "You do not have permission to delete this question"
}

docs.title: Get Unanswered Questions (Moderator or Admin)
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/questions/unanswered/

Query Parameters: - hub - Filter by hub ID - search - Search in title and body - page - Page number

Response (200 OK): Same as list questions, but only OPEN status

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "error": "You do not have permission to view unanswered questions"
}

A platform admin sees unanswered questions across every hub. A user with an active ModeratorAssignment or SchoolRepresentativeAssignment for a hub sees unanswered questions belonging to that hub, this includes a freshly-activated hub with representatives assigned but no moderator yet. A user with none of these is blocked with a 403.

docs.title: Follow Question
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/follow/

Response (201 Created):

{
  "message": "Now following question",
  "is_following": true
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "You are already following this question"
}

docs.title: Unfollow Question
docs.text:
Endpoint: DELETE /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/follow/

Response (204 No Content): Empty

Error Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "You have not followed this question"
}

Following is independent of authorship, a question's own author can follow their own question but doesn't need to, they already receive notifications for it by default. Followers get an in-app-only NEW_ANSWER notification (varied message text, no new notification type) when the question receives a new answer or when a best answer is marked, excluding whichever user is already notified through the existing author-facing paths. No follower count is exposed anywhere in the API, is_following reflects only the requesting user's own follow state.

docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/answers/

Rate limited to 50 requests per hour per user (see Rate Limits below).

Request:

{
  "question_id": "uuid",
  "body": "To calculate your CGPA, you need to..."
}

Response (201 Created):

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "body": "To calculate your CGPA, you need to...",
  "question": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "title": "How do I calculate my CGPA?"
  },

    "id": "uuid",

    "avatar": "https://..."

  "updated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"

Error Responses:

// 400 Bad Request
{
  "question_id": ["This field is required."],
  "body": ["This field is required."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - Question Locked
{
  "question_id": ["This question is locked and does not accept new answers."]
}

Answering someone else's question sends them a NEW_ANSWER notification (in-app and email), regardless of the question's current status. Answers can be added to a question at any status, including SOLVED, see the Update Question note below on what SOLVED actually means. Followers of the question (see Follow Question above) also receive an in-app-only NEW_ANSWER notification, excluding the answering user and the question author.

docs.title: Update Answer
docs.text:
Endpoint: PATCH /api/v1/answers/{answer_id}/

Request:

{
  "body": "Updated answer content"

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

docs.title: Delete Answer
docs.text:
Endpoint: DELETE /api/v1/answers/{answer_id}/

Response (204 No Content): Empty

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "error": "You do not have permission to delete this answer"
}

If the deleted answer was the question's best answer and other answers remain, the question's status reverts from SOLVED to ANSWERED. If it was the last remaining answer on the question, status reverts to OPEN.

docs.title: Mark Best Answer
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/answers/{answer_id}/mark-best/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "message": "Answer marked as best",
  "answer": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "is_best": true
  },
  "question": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "status": "SOLVED"
  }
}

Error Responses:

// 403 Forbidden - Not the question owner
{
  "error": "Only the question owner can mark a best answer"
}

// 400 Bad Request - Answer already marked as best
{
  "error": "This answer is already marked as best"
}

Marking a different answer as best on an already-solved question transfers the best-answer flag to the new answer and leaves the question SOLVED. Only marking the same answer that is already best is blocked. If the newly marked answer belongs to someone other than the question owner, they receive a BEST_ANSWER notification (in-app and email). Followers of the question also receive an in-app-only NEW_ANSWER notification, excluding the question owner and the marked answer's author.

docs.title: Vote on Answer
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/answers/{answer_id}/vote/

Rate limited to 100 requests per hour per user, shared with Remove Vote below (see Rate Limits below).

Request:

{
  "vote_type": "UP"
}

Response (200 OK):

{
  "message": "Vote recorded",
  "vote_type": "UP",
  "vote_score": 15

Error Responses:

// 400 Bad Request - Already voted
{
  "error": "You have already voted on this answer"
}

// 400 Bad Request - Can't vote on own answer

  "error": "You cannot vote on your own answer"
}

// 400 Bad Request - Invalid vote type
{
  "vote_type": ["This field must be one of: UP, DOWN."]
}

Voting sends the answer's author a VOTE notification, in-app only, no email. There is no dedicated "change my vote" endpoint, remove your existing vote first, then vote again with the new type.

user_vote ("UP", "DOWN", or null) appears on every answer object returned from Get Question, Create Answer, and Update Answer, reflecting the requesting user's own vote on that specific answer. It is always null for anonymous requests, and always null on an answer's own author (self-voting is blocked). Use this to restore vote-button state correctly on page load, without it the frontend would only know about votes cast during the current session.

docs.title: List Tags
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/tags/

Query Parameters: - search - Search by tag name - popular - Sort by question count (true/false), ties broken by name - page - Page number (default: 1) - page_size - Items per page (default: 50, max: 100)

Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 120,
  "next": "https://api.academia.com/api/v1/tags/?page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "gpa",
      "question_count": 25
    },
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "admission",
      "question_count": 18
    }
  ]
}

Tag names are normalized to lowercase everywhere, on creation, search, and every filter, so "GPA" and "gpa" are always treated as the same tag. Results are ordered alphabetically, or by question count with popular=true, with the name as a tiebreaker so pages never overlap. Requesting a page past the end returns a 404. This endpoint was unpaginated before: the new envelope is a superset of the old {"results": [...]} shape, but a client that assumed it received every tag now only sees the first page.

Caching & Visibility Behavior: - Cache: Public requests are cached using tag-list:<query_params> key for CACHE_TTL_SHORT (60 seconds), page and page_size included. - Invalidation: Cleared when a tag is merged, renamed, or deleted. New tags created implicitly through question tagging appear when the TTL expires.

docs.title: Get Questions by Tag
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/tags/{tag_name}/questions/

Query Parameters: - Same as list questions

Response (200 OK): Same as list questions. A tag name with no matching questions returns 200 OK with an empty result set, not a 404, consistent with how every other query-param filter on this API behaves.

docs.title: Delete Tag (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: DELETE /api/v1/tags/{tag_id}/

Query Parameters: - force - true to delete a tag that still has questions attached (default: not forced)

Response (204 No Content): Empty

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "This tag is attached to 12 questions. Pass ?force=true to delete it anyway."
}

Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "Tag not found"
}

By default, deleting a tag that's still attached to any question is blocked, to avoid silently orphaning content. Pass ?force=true to delete it anyway, this removes the tag from every question it's on (via cascade on QuestionTag), it does not delete the questions themselves.

Invalidation Note: Invalidates the tag-list cache prefix.

This action is recorded in the admin action log (visible in Django admin).

docs.title: Merge Tag (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/tags/{tag_id}/merge/

Merges the tag in the URL (the source) into a target tag, reassigning every question tagged with the source over to the target, then removes the source tag. The target can be specified two ways:

Request, merge into an existing tag:

{
  "target_tag_id": "uuid"
}

Request, rename (or merge-by-name):

{
  "target_name": "siwes"
}

Exactly one of target_tag_id / target_name must be provided. When target_name is given: if a tag with that name (after lowercase normalization) already exists, this behaves identically to target_tag_id, a real merge. If no tag with that name exists yet, the source tag is simply renamed in place, a rename is just a merge into a name nobody holds yet, so there is no separate rename endpoint.

Response (200 OK), merge:

{
  "message": "Tags merged successfully",
  "tag": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "name": "siwes",
    "question_count": 40
  },
  "questions_reassigned": 15
}

Response (200 OK), rename:

{
  "message": "Tag renamed successfully",
  "tag": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "name": "siwes",
    "question_count": 12
  }
}

questions_reassigned only appears on the merge response, and counts questions actually moved over, if a question already carried both the source and target tag, its duplicate source association is simply dropped rather than counted as a reassignment.

Error Responses:

// 400 Bad Request - Neither field provided
{
  "error": "Provide either target_tag_id or target_name."
}

// 400 Bad Request - Both fields provided
{
  "error": "Provide only one of target_tag_id or target_name, not both."
}

// 400 Bad Request - Merging a tag into itself
{
  "error": "Cannot merge a tag into itself."
}

// 400 Bad Request - target_tag_id doesn't exist
{
  "target_tag_id": ["Tag with this ID does not exist."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - Malformed target_tag_id
{
  "error": "Invalid ID format"
}

// 400 Bad Request - target_name too long
{
  "target_name": ["Tag names must be 50 characters or fewer."]
}

Response (404 Not Found):

{
  "error": "Tag not found"
}

Invalidation Note: Invalidates the tag-list cache prefix.

This action is recorded in the admin action log (visible in Django admin).

docs.title: Search Questions
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/search/questions/

Rate limited to 60 requests per minute (see Rate Limits below).

Query Parameters: - q - Search query - hub - Filter by hub ID - school - Filter by school ID - department - Filter by department ID - tag - Filter by tag name - page - Page number

Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 45,
  "next": "https://api.academia.com/api/v1/search/questions/?page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "title": "How do I calculate my CGPA?",
      "slug": "how-do-i-calculate-my-cgpa",
      "body": "I'm confused about the grading system...",
      "status": "SOLVED",
      "score": 0.4213,
      "author": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "full_name": "John Doe",
        "avatar": "https://..."
      },
      "hub": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "school": {
          "name": "University of Lagos",
          "short_name": "UNILAG",
          "slug": "unilag"
        }
      },
      "tags": ["gpa", "grading"],
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

Note: Results are ranked by: 1. Solved questions (status=SOLVED) with best answers 2. Highly voted answers 3. Recent content 4. Relevance to search terms

score is a raw PostgreSQL ts_rank value, higher means more textually relevant, but it has no fixed upper bound (it is not a normalized 0 to 1 percentage). It is null whenever q is omitted, since relevance has no meaning without a query to rank against, in that case results still return, ordered by the first three ranking priorities above.

When q is given, rows with a text rank below 0.0001 are excluded. PostgreSQL returns about 1e-20 for non-matches on multi-term queries, so without this floor q would not filter.

Caching & Visibility Behavior: - Cache: Public requests are cached using search-questions:<query_params> key for CACHE_TTL_SEARCH (30 seconds). - Invalidation: TTL expiry only, no active invalidation trigger exists for search results, given the short TTL and the volume of writes (new answers, votes, status changes) that could affect ranking, active invalidation wasn't worth the complexity.

docs.title: List Notifications
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/notifications/

Query Parameters: - is_read - true/false - page - Page number

Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 25,
  "unread_count": 5,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "type": "NEW_COMMENT",
      "message": "Jane Smith commented on your answer",
      "is_read": false,
      "related_object_id": "uuid",
      "related_object_type": "answer",
      "link_target": {
        "question_id": "uuid",
        "question_slug": "how-do-i-calculate-my-cgpa",
        "answer_id": "uuid"
      },
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

related_object_type/related_object_id are serialized from the underlying ContentType-based generic relation (see database-schema.md), the JSON shape doesn't change even as new notifiable models are added.

Notification types currently triggered: NEW_ANSWER (email and in-app), BEST_ANSWER (email and in-app), HUB_ACTIVATED (email and in-app), NEW_COMMENT (in-app only), VOTE (in-app only), MODERATOR_ASSIGNED (in-app only, fires for both moderator and representative assignment), NEW_QUESTION (in-app only, sent to every active moderator AND representative of the hub a new question is posted in, excluding the question's own author, deduplicated if a user holds both roles), NEW_ACTIVATION_REQUEST (in-app only, sent to every active admin when a new hub activation request is submitted, excluding the requester if they happen to be an admin), NEW_REPORT (in-app only, sent to every active admin when a new report is submitted, excluding the reporter if they happen to be an admin), USER_SUSPENDED (email and in-app, fires only on the transition from active to suspended, not on a repeated suspend call or on reactivation), HUB_ACTIVATION_REJECTED (email and in-app, sent to the original requester when their activation request is rejected), REPORT_REVIEWED (in-app only, sent to the original reporter when their report is resolved or rejected, excluding the reporter if they happen to be the reviewing admin).

link_target says where to send the user: the question page, optionally anchored to an answer, e.g. /questions/{question_id}/{question_slug}#answer-{answer_id}. It is set when the related object is a question, answer, or comment. For a comment, answer_id is the comment's parent answer (comments render inside their answer). It is null when there is nothing to link to: hubs, activation requests, reports, account notices, or content that has since been deleted. page_size is supported (default 20, max 100).

docs.title: Create Report
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/reports/

Rate limited to 10 requests per hour per user (see Rate Limits below).

Request:

{
  "content_type": "question",
  "content_id": "uuid",
  "type": "SPAM",
  "description": "This appears to be promotional content"
}

Response (201 Created):

{
  "id": "uuid",
  "content_type": "question",
  "content_id": "uuid",
  "type": "SPAM",
  "description": "This appears to be promotional content",
  "status": "PENDING",
  "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

content_type/content_id are serialized from the underlying ContentType-based generic relation (see database-schema.md), the JSON shape stays stable even as new reportable models (e.g. SchoolReview) are added later. Supported values for content_type are question, answer, and comment.

Error Responses:

// 400 Bad Request - Already reported by this user
{
  "error": "You have already reported this content"
}

// 400 Bad Request - Invalid content_type
{
  "content_type": ["content_type must be one of: question, answer, comment."]
}

// 400 Bad Request - No matching content
{
  "content_id": ["No matching content found for this content_type and content_id."]
}

Submitting a report sends every active admin a NEW_REPORT notification, in-app only, excluding the reporter if they happen to be an admin. The notification message includes the report's type for quick triage from the notification list itself, without needing to open the report first.

A user cannot report the same piece of content more than once, this restriction applies regardless of whether an earlier report on that content was resolved or rejected.

docs.title: List Reports (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/reports/

Query Parameters: - status - PENDING/RESOLVED/REJECTED - is_escalated - true/false - content_type - question/answer/comment. An unrecognized value returns a 400 with the same message as Create Report's content_type error - page - Page number

Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 10,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "content_type": "question",
      "content_id": "uuid",
      "type": "SPAM",
      "description": "This appears to be promotional content",
      "status": "PENDING",
      "reporter": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "full_name": "John Doe"
      },
      "is_escalated": false,
      "escalated_by": null,
      "content_exists": true,
      "link_target": {
        "question_id": "uuid",
        "question_slug": "how-do-i-calculate-my-cgpa",
        "answer_id": "uuid"
      },
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

content_exists is false when the reported content has since been deleted by a path that doesn't auto-resolve its reports (for example an author deleting their own question). Such a report stays PENDING until an admin rejects it or resolves it, resolving with DELETE_CONTENT is safe, it simply finds nothing to delete.

link_target has the same shape and meaning as on notifications: the question, plus the answer to anchor to when the reported content is an answer or a comment. It is null whenever content_exists is false.

docs.title: List My Reports
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/reports/mine/

Requires authentication. Returns only reports the requesting user filed, newest first, so a reporter can see whether anything came of them. It is deliberately minimal and self-scoped: there is no way to see another user's reports, and nothing about the review itself (who reviewed it, whether a moderator escalated it) is exposed, since reports are private in both directions.

Query Parameters: - status - PENDING/RESOLVED/REJECTED - page - Page number - page_size - Items per page

Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 4,
  "next": null,
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "content_type": "question",
      "content_id": "uuid",
      "type": "SPAM",
      "description": "This appears to be promotional content",
      "status": "RESOLVED",
      "resolved_at": "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z",
      "content_exists": true,
      "link_target": {
        "question_id": "uuid",
        "question_slug": "how-do-i-calculate-my-cgpa",
        "answer_id": null
      },
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

resolved_at is null while a report is PENDING. content_exists and link_target have the same meaning as on the admin list: link_target is null once the content is gone. A RESOLVED report does not necessarily mean content was removed, resolving can acknowledge a report without taking action, use content_exists to tell.

docs.title: Resolve Report (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/reports/{report_id}/resolve/

Request:

{
  "action": "DELETE_CONTENT"
}

Response (200 OK):

{
  "message": "Report resolved",
  "status": "RESOLVED",
  "action_taken": "DELETE_CONTENT",
  "auto_resolved_count": 3,
  "resolved_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "This report has already been reviewed"
}

Resolving sends the original reporter a REPORT_REVIEWED notification, in-app only, excluding the reporter if they are also the resolving admin.

When action is DELETE_CONTENT, every other PENDING report pointing at the deleted content, or at answers and comments removed along with it by cascade (deleting a question removes its answers and their comments), is resolved in the same request. Their reporters receive the same REPORT_REVIEWED notification, excluding the resolving admin. auto_resolved_count says how many were closed this way, 0 for any other action. The resolution is recorded in the admin action log.

action: "DELETE_CONTENT" is the only value with special behavior, it deletes the underlying reported object. Any other value, or omitting action entirely, resolves the report without taking any action on the content itself, useful when a report is valid to acknowledge but doesn't warrant removal.

docs.title: Reject Report (Admin Only)
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/reports/{report_id}/reject/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "message": "Report rejected",
  "status": "REJECTED",
  "resolved_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "This report has already been reviewed"
}

Rejecting sends the original reporter a REPORT_REVIEWED notification, in-app only, excluding the reporter if they are also the rejecting admin.

This action is recorded in the admin action log (visible in Django admin).

docs.title: Escalate Report
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/reports/{report_id}/escalate/

Restricted to an active Moderator or Representative for the reported content's hub, or an admin. Marks an existing PENDING report as escalated, signaling that a staff member's judgment (not just a student complaint) flagged it for priority review. Requires an existing report, there is no way to escalate unreported content directly, file a report first via POST /reports/ then escalate it.

Response (200 OK):

{

docs.title: List Pages
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/v1/pages/

Response (200 OK):

{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "title": "Privacy Policy",
      "slug": "privacy-policy",
      "visibility": "PUBLIC",
      "is_published": true,
      "created_by": { "id": "uuid", "full_name": "Jane Admin" },
      "updated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

Not paginated, low volume. Visibility is computed per requester: - Anonymous or plain authenticated users see published PUBLIC pages only. - Staff (is_admin, or an active moderator/representative assignment for any hub) additionally see published STAFF pages. - Admins see everything, including unpublished drafts of either visibility.

created_by is null if the creating user's account has since been deleted.

Caching Behavior: - Cache: Responses for anonymous/plain users and for staff are cached separately (two visibility tiers, never per user), using CACHE_TTL_MEDIUM (300 seconds). The tier is part of every cache key, so a page visible only to staff can never be served to a public request. - Admin Bypass: Admins always read live data, including drafts, and never populate the shared cache. - Invalidation: Creating, updating, or deleting a page clears its cached list and detail entries for both tiers immediately. A 404 is never cached.

A 404 is never cached.

docs.title: ID Format Validation
docs.text:
Every path parameter that identifies a resource (school, hub, question, answer, comment, notification, report, department, activation request, user) is validated as a well-formed UUID before any lookup happens. A malformed ID (wrong length, invalid characters, etc.) returns a 400, distinct from a well-formed ID that simply doesn't match anything, which still returns the resource's documented 404. Body fields that identify a resource, such as target_tag_id on Merge Tag, are validated the same way and return the same 400.

Response (400 Bad Request):

{
  "error": "Invalid ID format"
}

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text:
Rate limits are enforced, not just documented. Limits are tracked per authenticated user where the request carries a valid access token, and per IP address for anonymous requests.

Endpoint Limit Authentication (login/refresh) 10 requests per minute Question creation 30 requests per hour Answer creation 50 requests per hour Comment creation 50 requests per hour Edit or delete an answer or comment (one shared pool) 60 requests per hour Mark best answer 30 requests per hour Voting (vote and remove-vote combined) 100 requests per hour Search (question search and user search share one pool) 60 requests per minute Reports 10 requests per hour General API (everything else) 100 requests per minute

The scoped limits above (authentication, question/answer/comment creation, voting, search, reports) apply in place of the general limit for that specific action, not in addition to it. Reading data (GET requests) is never subject to the tighter write-action limits, only the general 100 per minute baseline applies to reads.

The edit/delete limit counts PATCH and DELETE on both answers and comments against a single per-user pool. Mark best answer is limited more tightly because each successful call can send an email and follower notifications. School, Department, and Static Page creation are intentionally left on the general 100 per minute baseline: all three are restricted to admins or school representatives, so they are not open to abuse by ordinary accounts.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
All list endpoints support pagination with the following parameters: - page: Page number (default: 1) - page_size: Items per page (default: 20, max: 100)

Response includes: - count: Total number of items - next: URL to next page (or null) - previous: URL to previous page (or null) - results: Array of items

docs.title: Backend Map
docs.text:
A file-oriented guide to backend/: where the API's behavior lives and how its apps work together. Use it with the other maintained references:

Document Question it answers API Contract What endpoints accept and return, error shapes, permissions and rate limits Database Schema Models, fields, constraints, indexes and relationships Backend Build Log Why implementation choices were made, conventions and deviations Feature List Which capabilities exist, are incomplete or remain planned

This map describes the current code organization. It is not a second API contract, schema reference or feature checklist.

docs.title: 1. Stack and local commands
docs.text:
• Django 6.0.6 on Python 3.12, Django REST Framework, SimpleJWT with refresh rotation and blacklist, PostgreSQL through psycopg 3, django-environ, django-redis, django-cors-headers, WhiteNoise and Gunicorn.
  • The product backend is a JSON API mounted under /api/v1/. Django admin is available separately under /admin/.
  • Run commands from backend/:
Command Purpose python manage.py runserver Local development server, defaults to development settings make run-lan Development server on 0.0.0.0:8000, for device testing on the LAN make test Run Django's discovered test suite make migrate Apply migrations python manage.py seed_demo_data Seed development data; see the data-command notes below before using --clear python manage.py print_test_tokens Print short-lived local test JWTs, DEBUG only python manage.py import_school_directory --dry-run Preview the regulator-directory import

manage.py, config/wsgi.py and config/asgi.py default to config.settings.development. Production must explicitly select config.settings.production with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE.

docs.title: 2. Project and settings files
docs.text: Path Responsibility manage.py Django management-command entry point config/urls.py Registers the loose-ID converter, mounts each API app at /api/v1/, and defines JSON API 404/500 handlers config/settings/base.py Installed apps, middleware, templates, database, cache, CORS, authentication, default permissions, throttles, JWT lifetimes and logging config/settings/development.py Debug mode, loopback hosts plus DJANGO_DEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS, local SMTP at port 1025 config/settings/production.py Production host/security settings, refuses SQLite unless explicitly allowed, JSON-only DRF renderer, SMTP and static/media storage configuration config/wsgi.py WSGI server entry point config/asgi.py ASGI server entry point requirements.txt Runtime dependencies Makefile Common run, migrate, shell, seed and test targets .env.example Environment variable names and local/deployment configuration notes templates/emails/ Shared email base plus HTML and plain-text notification templates

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
backend/.env.example is authoritative for environment-variable names.

Variable Purpose and behavior DJANGO_SECRET_KEY Required Django secret DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE Settings module; entry points default to development DATABASE_URL Database connection; local development falls back to db.sqlite3 when unset DATABASE_CONN_MAX_AGE Persistent database connection lifetime; use 0 with the serverless transaction pooler DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS, CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS Production host and origin lists DJANGO_DEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS Additional development hosts, such as a LAN address for Expo Go DJANGO_ALLOW_SQLITE Explicit opt-in for SQLite under production settings, used by the preview deployment REDIS_URL Optional Redis cache; unset uses per-process local memory CACHE_TTL_SHORT, CACHE_TTL_MEDIUM, CACHE_TTL_SEARCH Cache durations, defaulting to 60, 300 and 30 seconds CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Comma-separated origins; native requests do not use CORS, Expo web preview does FRONTEND_URL Base URL used for email links EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_PORT, EMAIL_HOST_USER, EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD, EMAIL_USE_TLS, DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL Production mail transport and sender SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS Production HTTPS redirect and HSTS duration DJANGO_LOG_LEVEL Root logger threshold, defaults to INFO DEFAULT_FILE_STORAGE_BACKEND Optional storage backend override; configure durable cloud storage before introducing uploads

The Django setting names SECRET_KEY and ALLOWED_HOSTS are populated from DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Email environment-variable names match Django's EMAIL_* settings; DEFAULT_FILE_STORAGE_BACKEND selects the STORAGES["default"]["BACKEND"] value.

docs.title: 3. Request and response flow
docs.text:
Client
  -> security, WhiteNoise and CORS middleware
  -> DRF authentication
  -> throttle
  -> explicit view permission
  -> view and serializer validation
  -> database write
  -> view-layer notifications, email and audit records
  -> response
  • Google access tokens are checked against Google's userinfo endpoint. Successful login returns Academia Atlas JWTs; there is no client secret or django-allauth flow. SimpleJWT rotates refresh tokens and blacklists used tokens.
  • DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES is intentionally AllowAny because public reads are common. Every view must declare its own permission classes. Client role fields are for display only; the backend checks every protected write.
  • apps.core.exceptions.custom_exception_handler normalizes general DRF errors and throttling responses. Field-specific 400 responses remain field-keyed.
  • Route IDs use the registered looseid converter so malformed IDs reach the view's UUID validation and return the documented 400 instead of a route 404. A valid but missing ID returns 404.
  • Notification and email side effects are initiated by views/services after successful writes, not by model signals. Audit writes are made in the same transaction as the action. Aggregate counters use targeted updates.
  • The frontend calls through its Next.js proxy and httpOnly cookies; mobile calls the API directly with bearer tokens in secure storage. Both use this same contract.

docs.title: 4. App and file map
docs.text: Every app has an apps.py registration module and a migrations/ package. The entries below list the files that implement behavior, not routine __init__.py or migration files. All inspected app tests.py files are placeholders rather than substantive per-app test suites.

docs.title: apps.accounts
docs.text:
Owns the custom user identity, Google login and user-facing account endpoints. The user distinguishes platform is_admin from Django is_staff.

File Responsibility models.py UUID-keyed User model, email identity and role/account flags managers.py UserManager: normalize email, set unusable passwords when omitted, and apply staff/admin defaults serializers.py UserSerializer includes hub-role summaries and computed activity counts; admin, update and user-picker representations use separate serializers views.py Google userinfo verification and JWT response; throttled refresh; refresh-token blacklist logout; current-user read/name update; admin user search/list/status change; active-user search for staff pickers urls.py auth/google/, auth/refresh/, auth/logout/, users/me/, users/search/, admin/users/ and user detail pagination.py UserPagination, 20 by default, maximum 100 admin.py Custom Django UserAdmin tests.py Placeholder; no substantive account-app tests found

Suspending/reactivating a user is an admin action. A real suspension transition is logged and sends the user a notification; repeated state-setting does not create a second transition record.

docs.title: apps.core
docs.text:
Shared API infrastructure and utilities used across apps. AdminActionLog is read-only in Django admin and does not have a public API endpoint.

File Responsibility models.py AdminActionLog, an append-only record with actor, action, UUID target, label snapshot and metadata audit.py log_admin_action(), called in the same transaction as the action admin.py Read-only audit-log admin permissions.py user_is_platform_admin() and IsPlatformAdmin utils.py UUID parsing and validation helpers converters.py LooseIDConverter, defers ID-format validation to the view slugs.py Unique persisted slug generation with collision retry, plus cosmetic display-slug handling cache.py Cache-key creation, safe get/set/delete, prefix invalidation and cached-response helper; cache failures log and fail open exceptions.py custom_exception_handler() for normalized DRF and throttle errors throttling.py MethodScopedThrottle, applies a throttle scope only to selected HTTP methods content_links.py get_link_target() maps questions, answers and comments to question/answer link identifiers views.py, urls.py health_check() probes database and cache; only database failure makes health degraded management/commands/seed_demo_data.py Seeds related development content across apps; supports reset and admin-email options management/commands/print_test_tokens.py Generates one-hour tokens for fixed local test users only when DEBUG=True management/commands/import_school_directory.py Imports school and provenance CSVs, supports dry run, matches by short name/name, fills blank fields, creates unmatched schools inactive, and writes source records idempotently tests.py Placeholder; no substantive core tests found

The directory import command currently does not expose source records through an API or mark old source records non-current. School curation fields and provenance are detailed in the schema and its open work is tracked in the feature list.

docs.text:
Owns platform-managed schools, departments and regulator-source provenance.

File Responsibility models.py School, Department and SchoolSourceRecord; stable school slug, computed active-hub state, school/department relationships and source provenance serializers.py School list/detail/write serializers; department list/create/update serializers; source-record serializer, currently not exposed by a view views.py Public school and department reads; search and school filters; admin school create/update and inactive-school visibility; representative department create/update; slug lookup urls.py School list, ID and slug details; nested department list/create; department detail cache.py invalidate_school_cache() clears list, detail and slug keys; called when hub activity changes computed School.has_hub pagination.py 20 by default, maximum 100 admin.py School and department admin, school-source records inline tests.py Placeholder; no substantive school-app tests found

School reads are public for active records. Platform admins can inspect inactive records. Department reads show active departments publicly and allow representatives/admins to manage the school’s departments.

docs.title: apps.hubs
docs.text:
Owns school hubs, activation requests and staff assignments.

File Responsibility models.py One-to-one Hub per school, HubActivationRequest, ModeratorAssignment and SchoolRepresentativeAssignment serializers.py Hub/school/department summaries, activation request input/output and role-assignment representations; validates inactive or already-served schools and duplicate pending requests permissions.py Hub/school-scoped moderator and representative checks, any-hub representative check, and shared user_is_staff() role check views.py Public hub detail/by-school/by-slug reads; admin activity toggle and audit; user activation request and admin review; moderator and representative list/assign/deactivate; role and hub notifications urls.py hubs/, activation request review, by-school and by-slug lookups, hub detail, nested moderators and representatives pagination.py Activation requests, 20 by default, maximum 100 admin.py Admin registrations for hub, requests and both assignment models tests.py Placeholder; no substantive hub-app tests found

Hub activation invalidates both hub and school caches. Assignment records use active flags rather than hard deletion, preserving a team across hub deactivation.

docs.title: apps.questions
docs.text:
Owns questions, follows and question-level staff actions.

File Responsibility models.py UUID question and follow models; status, hub, optional department, lock/view fields, answer count, best-answer ID and tag access serializers.py List/detail and create/update serializers; detail nests answers and follow state; _sync_tags() normalizes and synchronizes tag links views.py Public list/detail, authenticated create, author-only edit/delete, staff unanswered queue, follow/unfollow and staff lock/unlock; authenticated view counts are deduplicated per-user over a rolling 24-hour cache window services.py notify_followers_of_new_answer() and best-answer follower notifications, excluding the question author and answer author where appropriate urls.py Question list/detail, unanswered, follow and lock routes pagination.py 20 by default, page_size supported, maximum 50 admin.py QuestionAdmin tests.py Placeholder; no substantive question-app tests found

Creation notifies active moderators and representatives assigned to the hub. Question create/update synchronizes tags through apps.tags. Detail serialization uses the answer serializers. Answer creation and best-answer selection call the follower notification service.

docs.title: apps.answers
docs.text:
Owns answers, votes and best-answer transitions.

File Responsibility models.py Answer and unique-per-user/per-answer AnswerVote; best-answer and vote-score fields, computed comment count serializers.py Answer author/question summaries, nested answer response and create/update validation; rejects missing or locked questions and advances an open question to answered views.py Create, author-only edit/delete, vote/unvote, question-owner best-answer marking and the current user’s answer list urls.py Answer list/create/detail, vote, mark-best and users/me/answers/ pagination.py 20 by default, maximum 50 admin.py Answer and vote model registration tests.py Placeholder; no substantive answer-app tests found

Votes reject self-voting and update the score. Marking best sets the question to solved. Deleting its last answer reopens it; deleting the best answer while other answers remain returns it to answered. Creation and best-answer actions notify the relevant author and followers; vote events create in-app notifications. The answer serializer is also used in question details.
