docs.title: apps.tags
docs.text:
Owns normalized tag names, question-tag joins and admin tag maintenance.

File Responsibility models.py Unique-name Tag and unique QuestionTag relation serializers.py Tag representation; uses an existing question-count annotation where available, otherwise counts related questions views.py Public list/search/popularity and tag-question list; admin-only delete and merge/rename utils.py Tag length limit and validate_tags() urls.py Tag list, merge, delete/detail and questions-by-tag routes pagination.py 50 by default, maximum 100 admin.py Tag and question-tag admin tests.py Placeholder; no substantive tag-app tests found

Delete is blocked when a tag is attached unless forced. Merge deduplicates question/tag links, records an admin action and invalidates the tag-list cache. Question serializers own synchronization of tags on question writes.

docs.title: apps.search
docs.text:
Provides the ranked question-search endpoint. It has no application models or schema migration.

File Responsibility views.py Public, throttled and cached question search; supports hub/school/department/tag filters and PostgreSQL full-text search serializers.py SearchQuestionSerializer, question search summary and rounded rank urls.py search/questions/ pagination.py 20 by default, maximum 50 admin.py No model registrations tests.py Placeholder; no substantive search-app tests found

With a nonempty q, ranking orders solved status, top answer vote score, creation time and then text rank. Without q, it orders by solved status, top vote score and creation time. The rank floor removes PostgreSQL's tiny non-match scores. Results query apps.questions.Question, filter QuestionTag, and reuse question summary serializers.

docs.title: apps.notifications
docs.text:
Owns in-app notification records, delivery helpers and read state.

File Responsibility models.py Typed Notification with a generic content-object reference serializers.py Notification representation, related object identifiers and shared link_target views.py Authenticated user-scoped list, optional read-state filter, unread count, mark-one-read and mark-all-read services.py create_notification(), send_notification_email() and notify(); email delivery failures are logged rather than raised urls.py Notification list, mark-all-read and mark-read routes pagination.py 20 by default, maximum 100 admin.py Notification admin tests.py Placeholder; no substantive notification-app tests found

Views prefetch common question/answer/comment targets. Notification side effects originate in the question, answer, comment, hub, account and report flows. The allowed types, channel policy and recipients are summarized in BUILD_LOG_BACKEND.md; exact response fields are in api-contract.md.

docs.title: apps.reports
docs.text:
Owns user reports and their admin review and staff escalation workflow.

File Responsibility models.py Report type/status, generic content target, reviewer/escalation fields and one-report-per-user/content uniqueness serializers.py Create response, admin report and private own-report forms; includes content-existence/link data while hiding review and escalation details from the reporter views.py Restricts targets to questions, answers and comments; authenticated report creation; admin list/resolve/reject; hub staff escalation; resolves target hub and deletion cascades; handles orphan reports and notifications urls.py Report create/list, own reports, resolve, reject and escalate pagination.py 20 by default, maximum 100 admin.py Report admin tests.py Placeholder; no substantive report-app tests found

Deleting reported content can cascade through answers/comments and auto-resolve related pending reports. Review/escalation actions log the appropriate admin action and notify relevant parties.

docs.title: apps.pages
docs.text:
Owns admin-managed policy, product and staff guide pages.

File Responsibility models.py StaticPage: generated unique slug, public/staff visibility, publish state, optional creator and timestamps serializers.py Author, list/detail and create/update representations; trims and validates titles views.py Public/admin list and detail; tiered public, staff and admin visibility; admin writes; per-tier caches and invalidation urls.py pages/ and pages/<identifier>/ admin.py StaticPageAdmin tests.py Placeholder; no substantive page-app tests found

Admins see drafts and all pages. Staff means an active moderator or representative and includes all published pages; other visitors see only published public pages. Reads return the same 404 for nonexistent and invisible pages. Detail GET uses the slug while PATCH/DELETE use the UUID on the same route shape.

docs.title: 5. Route map
docs.text:
config/urls.py mounts the route groups below at /api/v1/. This table is a navigation aid; request and response schemas, complete permission behavior and errors are defined in the API Contract.

Auth labels: public means no login required, user means any authenticated account, staff means moderator/representative for the relevant hub or admin, rep means representative for the relevant school or admin, and admin means platform admin.

App Route group Access and purpose core GET /health/ Public liveness/dependency check; only database failure marks service degraded accounts POST /auth/google/, /auth/refresh/ Public login/refresh, auth throttle accounts POST /auth/logout/ User; blacklist current refresh token accounts GET, PATCH /users/me/ User profile, role summaries, stats and name update accounts GET /users/search/ Admin or representative of any hub; bounded picker results accounts GET /admin/users/, GET and PATCH /admin/users/{id}/ Admin user search/detail and suspend/reactivate schools GET /schools/, GET /schools/{id}/ Public active directory/detail; admins can inspect inactive records on the ID route schools GET /schools/by-slug/{slug}/ Public active-school lookup; admins bypass the cache and can inspect inactive schools schools POST /schools/, PATCH /schools/{id}/ Admin create/update; deactivate through is_active schools GET, POST /schools/{id}/departments/, PATCH /departments/{id}/ Public reads; school representative/admin writes hubs GET /hubs/{id}/, /hubs/by-school/{id}/, /hubs/by-slug/{slug}/ Public active hub reads; admins can access inactive hubs hubs PATCH /hubs/{id}/ Admin activity toggle, audited on real transitions hubs GET, POST /hubs/activation-requests/, POST .../{id}/approve/, POST .../{id}/reject/ Authenticated request; admin list and review hubs GET, POST /hubs/{id}/moderators/, DELETE .../{user_id}/ Public active list; representative/admin assignment and removal hubs GET, POST /hubs/{id}/representatives/, DELETE .../{user_id}/ Public active list; admin assignment and removal questions GET, POST /questions/; GET, PATCH, DELETE /questions/{id}/ Public reads; authenticated create; author edit/delete questions GET /questions/unanswered/ Staff queue scoped to the user's hub roles questions POST, DELETE /questions/{id}/follow/; POST, DELETE /questions/{id}/lock/ User follow; staff lock/unlock answers POST /answers/, PATCH, DELETE /answers/{id}/ Authenticated create; author edit/delete answers POST, DELETE /answers/{id}/vote/; POST /answers/{id}/mark-best/ User vote; question author marks best answers GET /users/me/answers/ User's own answer history comments GET /answers/{id}/comments/, POST /comments/, PATCH, DELETE /comments/{id}/ Public list; authenticated create; author edit/delete comments GET /users/me/comments/ User's own comment history tags GET /tags/, GET /tags/{name}/questions/ Public paginated tag list and question list tags DELETE /tags/{id}/, POST /tags/{id}/merge/ Admin delete, merge or rename search GET /search/questions/ Public ranked search notifications GET /notifications/, POST /notifications/mark-all-read/, POST /notifications/{id}/mark-read/ User-scoped list and read state reports POST /reports/, GET /reports/mine/ User report creation and private report history reports GET /reports/, POST /reports/{id}/resolve/, /reject/ Admin review reports POST /reports/{id}/escalate/ Staff escalation for a hub report pages GET /pages/, GET /pages/{slug}/ Public/staff/admin visibility tiers pages POST /pages/, PATCH, DELETE /pages/{id}/ Admin page management

docs.title: Permissions and IDs
docs.text: Concern Implementation Platform administrator apps.core.permissions.user_is_platform_admin() and IsPlatformAdmin Hub roles apps.hubs.permissions helpers for moderator, representative and combined staff checks Method-specific throttling apps.core.throttling.MethodScopedThrottle Loose route IDs apps.core.converters.LooseIDConverter; views validate UUID syntax with core helpers Slugs apps.core.slugs generates persisted unique slugs and handles display-only URL slugs Generic content links apps.core.content_links.get_link_target() provides question and answer identifiers for report/notification links

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
Redis is used when REDIS_URL is set; otherwise Django's local-memory cache is used. Redis failures fail open: throttles do not block due to an unavailable cache and cache-backed views recompute. Cache keys and invalidation helpers are centralized in apps.core.cache; school invalidation is shared with apps.schools.cache.

Cached data Invalidation or expiry School lists and detail/by-slug data School writes; department and hub state changes also invalidate relevant school data Hub detail/by-school/by-slug Hub activity/update and team assignment changes Tag lists Tag delete, merge and rename Ranked question search Short TTL; no content-write invalidation Static pages Separate public/staff visibility tiers; writes invalidate, invisible 404s are not cached Authenticated question view dedup Per user, rolling 24-hour window; not a response cache

Live Q&A content and personalized responses are not cached as response objects. Refer to apps/*/cache.py and apps.core.cache when changing cache keys.

docs.title: Throttles
docs.text:
Rates are configured in config/settings/base.py, keyed by throttle scope. Authenticated requests are user-throttled and anonymous requests are IP-throttled. Scoped write limits replace the global limit for that action; they do not stack.

Scope Rate Default anonymous/user 100 per minute Authentication 10 per minute Question create 30 per hour Answer create, comment create 50 per hour each Content edit 60 per hour Mark best 30 per hour Voting 100 per hour Search 60 per minute Reports 10 per hour

A view that refers to an unconfigured throttle scope raises a server configuration error; define the matching rate in base.py.

docs.title: Notifications and email
docs.text:
apps.notifications.services is the shared delivery entry point. The recipient/channel matrix and full notification type list live in BUILD_LOG_BACKEND.md and api-contract.md, rather than being duplicated here.

Triggering area Examples of behavior Accounts Suspension notice; role assignment notice is sent by hubs Hubs New activation request to active admins; approval/rejection to requester; moderator and representative assignment Questions New question to active hub moderators and representatives; answer/best-answer follower notifications are coordinated with answers Answers New answer and best-answer notices to relevant authors; vote notice to answer author Comments New comment notice to answer author, unless self-authored Reports New report to admins; staff escalation; review outcome to reporter

Email templates are under templates/emails/. Development SMTP uses MailHog-compatible settings at localhost port 1025; production transport is environment configured. Email delivery errors are logged and do not undo a successful API write.

docs.title: 7. Data commands and source data
docs.text: Command or path Purpose and cautions apps/core/management/commands/seed_demo_data.py Seed schools, hubs, accounts, questions, answers, tags and pages. --clear cascades from schools and also clears tags/static pages; never use against a database holding the real directory. --admin-email promotes the specified account apps/core/management/commands/print_test_tokens.py Prints one-hour tokens for fixed admin, staff and regular test users; requires DEBUG=True apps/core/management/commands/import_school_directory.py Idempotent NUC/NBTE/NCCE import. Matches by short name then name, fills blank values and creates unmatched schools inactive for review. --dry-run previews; source records are written, but prior rows are not marked non-current apps/schools/data/ School import inputs and duplicate-review data; inspect the command and source files before running an import templates/emails/ Shared email base and per-notification HTML/plain-text templates

docs.title: 8. Testing and verification
docs.text:
make test runs Django's test discovery from backend/. At the time this map was verified, app tests.py modules are placeholders and do not provide substantive per-app regression coverage. Use Testing for the cross-surface manual regression checklist. For endpoint-level inputs, responses, permissions and errors, use API Contract.

Useful repository checks:

cd backend
python manage.py check
python manage.py showmigrations
make test

For local mobile device access, set DJANGO_DEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS to the device- reachable development host, include the Expo web preview in CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS when testing web, then run make run-lan.

docs.title: 9. Where to make a change
docs.text: Change Primary code path Documentation to update Endpoint or response behavior App serializers.py, views.py, urls.py, and relevant helper/service API Contract, Feature List if capability status changes, then Changelog Model, field or relationship App models.py and migration Database Schema, then Changelog Permission or role behavior View permission declaration and/or apps.hubs.permissions / apps.core.permissions API Contract and Backend Build Log Notification or email Triggering view/service, apps.notifications.services, templates as needed API Contract and Backend Build Log Cache behavior apps.core.cache and relevant app view/cache helper This map and Backend Build Log if convention changes Throttle behavior View throttle classes/scope and config/settings/base.py API Contract and this map School import apps/core/management/commands/import_school_directory.py and source inputs Feature List, Database Schema if data shape changes, Backend Build Log

docs.title: 10. Deferred work
docs.text: The current backend backlog and deliberate deviations are maintained in BUILD_LOG_BACKEND.md and feature-list.md. Check those references before treating an absent endpoint or behavior as an accidental omission. In particular, audit log read access, representative-scoped report visibility, answer edit history and durable upload storage are not documented here as implemented features.

docs.title: User
docs.text:
Represents an authenticated user on the platform.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier email String Unique, Required User email address full_name String Required User's full name avatar String Nullable URL to avatar image (from Google) is_active Boolean Default: True Account active status is_admin Boolean Default: False Platform administrator flag (checked by API views) is_staff Boolean Default: False Django admin-site login flag (separate from is_admin) created_at DateTime Auto now Account creation timestamp updated_at DateTime Auto now Last update timestamp

docs.title: School
docs.text:
Represents an educational institution.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier name String Unique, Required Full institution name short_name String Unique, Required Abbreviated name slug String Unique, Auto-generated URL-friendly identifier, generated once from short_name at creation, never regenerated on edit location String Nullable City/State location website String Nullable Official website URL verification_status Enum Default: UNVERIFIED UNVERIFIED/PENDING/VERIFIED is_active Boolean Default: True School active status (also used as soft-delete) institution_type Enum Nullable UNIVERSITY/POLYTECHNIC/COLLEGE_OF_EDUCATION. Deliberately kept to three values, see School Data Curation note below ownership Enum Nullable FEDERAL/STATE/PRIVATE state String Nullable Nigerian state, free text regulatory_code String Nullable, Unique Reserved for a JAMB institution code, not populated by the initial NUC/NBTE/NCCE import source_url String Nullable The regulator page this record's data was last confirmed against last_verified_at DateTime Nullable Set explicitly by the import process or an admin correction, not auto-derived country String Default: "Nigeria" Forward-compatible field for eventual multi-country expansion, no multi-country logic exists yet created_at DateTime Auto now Creation timestamp updated_at DateTime Auto now Last update timestamp

has_hub is not a stored field, it's computed from the related Hub record.

School Data Curation note on institution_type: source regulator data contains six raw categories (universities, polytechnics, colleges of education, allied institutions, colleges of health technology, colleges of nursing). Allied institutions, colleges of health technology, and colleges of nursing all collapse into POLYTECHNIC as their nearest general category, since all three are NBTE-regulated, sub-degree/technical institutions structurally closer to a polytechnic than to a university or a college of education. The original, more specific category string is preserved per-record on SchoolSourceRecord.raw_category below, nothing from the source is actually lost, it's just not promoted to a first-class School field.

docs.title: SchoolSourceRecord
docs.text:
Per-regulator provenance for a School, one row per source confirmation. Exists specifically to support "never auto-deactivate a School based on one source disappearing" (see project-plan.md's Schools Are Platform Data principle): a future re-pull of a regulator's list flips is_current to False here rather than touching School.is_active directly, leaving deactivation a deliberate, reviewed admin decision instead of an automatic side effect. No independent API endpoint, admin-visible only (inline under School in Django admin).

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier school ForeignKey(School) Required, CASCADE The school this record confirms regulator Enum Required NUC/NBTE/NCCE raw_category String Required The exact original source label (e.g. "Allied Institution", "College of Nursing"), preserved even though it's collapsed into a simpler School.institution_type raw_payload JSON Default: empty object VC/provost name, year established, anything else the source carried that isn't a dedicated School column source_url String Required The regulator page this record was sourced from fetched_at DateTime Required When this source data was pulled is_current Boolean Default: True Flipped False when a later re-pull of that regulator's list no longer finds this institution created_at DateTime Auto now Creation timestamp updated_at DateTime Auto now Last update timestamp

docs.text:
Represents a user following a question for update notifications, independent of authorship.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier user ForeignKey(User) Required, CASCADE Following user question ForeignKey(Question) Required, CASCADE Followed question created_at DateTime Auto now Follow timestamp

docs.title: Notification
docs.text:
Represents a notification for a user.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier user ForeignKey(User) Required, CASCADE Recipient type Enum Required NEW_ANSWER/NEW_COMMENT/NEW_QUESTION/BEST_ANSWER/VOTE/MODERATOR_ASSIGNED/HUB_ACTIVATED/NEW_ACTIVATION_REQUEST/NEW_REPORT/USER_SUSPENDED/HUB_ACTIVATION_REJECTED/REPORT_REVIEWED message String Required Notification text is_read Boolean Default: False Read status content_type ForeignKey(ContentType) Nullable Related object's model type (Django ContentType) object_id UUID Nullable Related object's ID created_at DateTime Auto now Notification timestamp

content_object is exposed via GenericForeignKey('content_type', 'object_id'). The public API still serializes this as related_object_type (string) / related_object_id (uuid), see api-contract.md.

docs.title: Report
docs.text:
Represents a user report on content.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier reporter ForeignKey(User) Required, CASCADE User who reported type Enum Required SPAM/ABUSE/MISINFORMATION/DUPLICATE content_type ForeignKey(ContentType) Required Reported object's model type (Django ContentType) object_id UUID Required ID of reported object description Text Nullable Additional context status Enum Default: PENDING PENDING/RESOLVED/REJECTED resolved_by ForeignKey(User) Nullable, SET_NULL Admin who resolved resolved_at DateTime Nullable Resolution timestamp is_escalated Boolean Default: False Set when a moderator or representative flags an existing report for priority admin review escalated_by ForeignKey(User) Nullable, SET_NULL Moderator/representative/admin who escalated created_at DateTime Auto now Creation timestamp updated_at DateTime Auto now Last update timestamp

Using Django's ContentType framework (instead of a plain string field) means any future model, including SchoolReview, can be reported without a schema change. The public API still serializes this as content_type: "question" / content_id: uuid.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier user ForeignKey(User) Required, CASCADE Assigned representative hub ForeignKey(Hub) Required, CASCADE Represented hub is_active Boolean Default: True Assignment active status created_at DateTime Auto now Assignment timestamp updated_at DateTime Auto now Last update timestamp

docs.title: StaticPage
docs.text:
Represents an admin-managed standalone content page (Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, staff onboarding guides, etc).

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier title String Required Page title slug String Unique, Auto-generated URL-friendly identifier, generated once from title at creation, never regenerated on edit, same pattern as School body Text Required Markdown source, rendered client-side visibility Enum Default: PUBLIC PUBLIC/STAFF is_published Boolean Default: False Draft status, unpublished pages are only visible to admins created_by ForeignKey(User) Nullable, SET_NULL Author. Nullable so deleting a user account never takes a page down with it created_at DateTime Auto now Creation timestamp updated_at DateTime Auto now Last update timestamp

"Staff" for visibility purposes means is_admin, or an active ModeratorAssignment/SchoolRepresentativeAssignment for any hub (checked globally, not scoped to a specific hub, since page visibility isn't hub-specific). Deleting a StaticPage is a genuine hard delete, unlike School/Department, since nothing else has a foreign key into it and draft/publish already covers the "hide without losing" case.

docs.title: AdminActionLog
docs.text:
Append-only record of privileged admin actions that otherwise leave no trace. Report and HubActivationRequest already store resolved_by / reviewed_by, this covers what had no record at all: who suspended or reactivated a user, who merged, renamed, or deleted a tag (the source tag no longer exists afterward), and which action was taken when resolving a report. Written by the API inside the same transaction as the action it records, visible and read-only in Django admin, no API endpoint. Lives in apps.core since it spans reports, accounts, and tags.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID Primary Key Unique identifier actor ForeignKey(User) Nullable, SET_NULL Admin who performed the action. Nullable so deleting an admin account never deletes the history action Enum Required REPORT_RESOLVED/REPORT_REJECTED/USER_SUSPENDED/USER_REACTIVATED/TAG_MERGED/TAG_RENAMED/TAG_DELETED target_type String Required report, user, or tag target_id UUID Required Plain UUID, not a foreign key, so an entry survives its target being deleted target_label String Blank allowed Human-readable snapshot taken at write time (tag name, user email, report summary) metadata JSON Default: empty object Action-specific detail, e.g. action_taken and auto_resolved_count for a resolved report, merged_into_name and questions_reassigned for a merge created_at DateTime Auto now When the action happened

Only genuine state changes are logged: a repeated suspend of an already suspended account, or a request blocked with a 400, writes nothing.

docs.title: Performance Indexes
docs.text:
• Question: (hub_id, created_at DESC) - For recent questions
  • Question: (hub_id, status) - For filtering by status
  • Question: (department_id) - For department filtering
  • Answer: (question_id, is_best) - For best answer lookup
  • AnswerVote: (answer_id) - For vote aggregation
  • Notification: (user_id, is_read, created_at DESC) - For user notifications
  • Notification: (content_type_id, object_id) - For generic relation lookups
  • Report: (status, created_at DESC) - For reports dashboard
  • Report: (content_type_id, object_id) - For generic relation lookups
  • Report: (is_escalated, created_at DESC) - For escalated reports triage
  • AdminActionLog: (target_type, target_id) - For looking up the history of one object
  • AdminActionLog: (actor_id, created_at DESC) - For looking up everything one admin did

docs.title: Unique Constraints
docs.text:
• School: name, short_name, slug, regulatory_code
  • Department: (school_id, name)
  • Hub: school_id
  • AnswerVote: (answer_id, user_id)
  • QuestionTag: (question_id, tag_id)
  • ModeratorAssignment: (user_id, hub_id)
  • SchoolRepresentativeAssignment: (user_id, hub_id)
  • APIClient: key_prefix

docs.title: Cascade Behavior
docs.text:
• Deleting a School → Delete associated Hub, Department, HubActivationRequest, SchoolSourceRecord
  • Deleting a Hub → Delete associated Question, ModeratorAssignment, SchoolRepresentativeAssignment
  • Deleting a User → Delete associated Question, Answer, Comment, Notification, Report
  • Deleting a User → AdminActionLog.actor is set to NULL, log entries are kept
  • Deleting a Question → Delete associated Answer, QuestionTag, QuestionFollow
  • Deleting an Answer → Delete associated Comment, AnswerVote
  • Deleting a Tag → Delete associated QuestionTag (only ever happens via explicit admin action, see api-contract.md's Delete Tag / Merge Tag)

In practice, School is not hard-deleted through the API, see api-contract.md's soft-delete note. Hard delete remains available at the database/admin level only.

docs.title: Design Guide
docs.text: The visual and interaction rules for Academia Atlas on web and mobile. Shared rules come first, then web and mobile specifics. Component and file locations are in frontend-map.md and mobile-map.md.

docs.title: Product and roles
docs.text:
Academia Atlas helps students ask academic questions specific to their school and preserves useful answers for future students. It is a searchable reference platform, not a social feed.

Role Capabilities Guest Browse and search schools, hubs, questions and answers. Cannot post, vote or comment User Guest capabilities, plus ask, answer, comment, vote, follow, request a hub, report content and receive notifications Moderator User capabilities, plus an unanswered queue for assigned hubs, lock and unlock, escalate School Representative User capabilities, plus department management and moderator assignment for their hub, lock and escalate Admin Manage schools, hub requests, representatives, reports, users, tags and static pages

The API contract defines the role fields. The backend is authoritative for every permission.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Function over decoration. Finding and contributing knowledge, not marketing.
  • Search before social. Browsing and filtering are the main navigation.
  • Content first. Questions and answers are the interface, metadata is small and muted.
  • Accessible by default. Visible focus, adequate contrast, and status is never conveyed by color alone: icons are paired with text.
  • Light and dark are equal. Neither theme is an afterthought.
  • Friendly failure. Every list and detail view handles loading, empty, error and populated states, with human copy.

docs.title: Color tokens
docs.text:
One accent, otherwise restrained and warm neutral. Both surfaces use the same values.

Token Light Dark Use bg #FBFAF8 #16171C Page and chrome background ink #16140F #F5F3EE Primary text border (line) #E5E3DF #2C2D34 Dividers, card edges border-strong #CFCBC2 #3A3B44 Form control and outlined button borders only muted #67645C #9EA1AB ALL secondary text surface #FFFFFF #1E2939 Inputs, cards, popovers, sheets accent #3454D1 #3454D1 Links, primary actions, focus ring, selected state success #1D8A6C #3FBF97 Solved state, confirmations danger #CE4747 #CE4747 Errors and destructive actions (web red scale is overridden to a clean red, 600 is #B93D3D)

Rules: - Muted is measured at 4.5:1 or better on every surface the app uses (about 5.7:1 on the page background). Never use raw grays for secondary text. - Control borders measure about 1.6:1, below WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1. This is a deliberate design trade-off. If stronger edges are wanted, retune only border-strong (candidates: light #8F8B80, dark #6B6D7A). - Tailwind's default gray scale is left untouched on web, and used for chips and hovers.

docs.title: Brand and app icons
docs.text: The logo is a blue "A" with a gold swoosh and four-point star. The blue is the UI accent #3454D1 and the gold is about #FFB000 (sample from the master). Gold appears only in the logo, app icon, splash and store graphics. The wordmark is "Academia" over "Atlas", the short form for tight spaces is "A-Atlas" (launcher label). Masters live in brand/src (mark-source, icon-source, tile-source, circle-source) and every PNG is generated by brand/make-brand-assets.sh. Icon rules: iOS icon opaque and square with no baked corners, Android adaptive mark inside the 61% safe zone on the accent background, monochrome icon a single-colour silhouette with a gap between the A and the swoosh.

docs.title: Typography
docs.text: Plus Jakarta Sans, weights 400 to 800, one family. Hierarchy comes from weight and size, not from extra families. Body 14 to 15px, meta 11 to 12px, page titles 20 to 30px extra-bold. Markdown content has its own typography (lists, quotes, code, headings only on static pages).

docs.title: Shape, spacing and layout
docs.text:
• Corners: standard radius for buttons, inputs and chips, a larger radius for cards, answer blocks and modals. Pill shape only for search bars. Circles only for avatars and count badges.
  • Lists are dividers, not cards: divide-y rows with a top and bottom border.
  • Web widths: main column max-w-5xl with px-4, question page max-w-3xl, forms max-w-2xl. Two-column layouts (filter sidebar plus list) start at md. The floating Ask button appears below sm.
  • Status is always icon plus label: open is an empty circle in muted, answered is a message icon in accent, solved is a check circle in success. Locked adds a lock in danger.

docs.title: Components and patterns
docs.text:
• Forms: label above the control, small and muted. Error under the field in danger. Backend field errors map to their own field. Sizes xs, sm, md, lg.
  • Messages: errors and warnings use one component with role alert. Empty states have an icon, a title and one line, never just gray text.
  • Menus: secondary actions (edit, delete, report, escalate, share) live in a kebab menu. Follow, vote and mark-best stay inline.
  • Confirmations: destructive actions confirm inline or in a small dialog, never silently.
  • Tabs scroll instead of wrapping and support arrow keys.
  • Platform badge: a small "A" mark next to the official account's name, tap to explain.
  • Markdown: all user content renders through one safe renderer.

docs.title: Motion and feedback
docs.text: Subtle and CSS-only. Buttons scale to 0.97 on press with 150ms transitions. Skeletons shimmer. Lists fade up with a short stagger, and rows added by "View more" animate on their own. The answer deep-link flash honors reduced motion. A global 2px accent focus ring with a 2px offset shows on keyboard focus.

docs.title: Stacking (web)
docs.text: z-dropdown 20, z-sticky 30, z-overlay 40, z-drawer 50, z-modal 60, z-toast 70, z-progress 100. New overlays pick a level, never a raw number.

docs.title: Theming
docs.text: Class-based dark mode. Web has a manual toggle in the top bar, persisted. Mobile follows the system by default with a manual override. Both must be checked on every change.

docs.title: Page states
docs.text: Every list or detail view handles loading (skeleton), empty, error with retry, and populated. Also: offline (mobile), expired session, and friendly copy for no network, 429 ("You're going a bit fast"), gateway timeouts and other 5xx. A 400 shows its message under the field.

docs.title: Web direction
docs.text: A structured, searchable reference tool. Compact question rows, prominent search on browsing pages, persistent filters in a sidebar that collapses on narrow screens. Top bar with wordmark, theme toggle, notification bell and profile menu. A sidebar drawer for navigation at every width. A homepage hero with a full-bleed background and a legibility scrim. Lucide icons.

docs.title: Mobile direction
docs.text:
Follows design/Mobile mockup, same tokens and typography. What differs from web:

Area Web Mobile Navigation Top bar plus overlay sidebar Bottom tabs (Home, Schools, Ask, Alerts with badge, Profile) plus a slide-over drawer Home school cards Side card list Horizontal strip of cards (tile, large question count, names, location) Google sign in Google Identity Services popup Native account picker (no browser redirect) Ask action Floating pill below sm, plus buttons on pages Raised centre tab Secondary actions Dropdown kebab menu Bottom sheet Modals Centered dialogs Bottom sheets, under 80% height, backdrop tap and swipe dismiss Sheets Centered dialogs Bottom sheets, backdrop tap and Back dismiss, swipe down planned Filters Collapsible sidebar Horizontal chips and a filter sheet Touch targets Pointer sized At least 44pt, bigger toolbar buttons in the editor Corners Standard and large radius 8pt controls, 12pt FAB, 16pt sheet tops Icons Lucide Font Awesome 6 equivalents, same meanings Avatars Not rendered Google photo with initial fallback Theme Manual toggle System by default, override in profile and drawer Feedback Hover and focus states Pressed states, pull to refresh, offline banner, reduced motion respected, text scaling capped at 1.4 Links Web URLs academiaatlas:// scheme, https links when set up, same paths as the web Keyboard n/a Composer and sheets stay above the keyboard Staff tools Full moderation and admin screens None. Lock, escalate and report in context, plus "Open on web" buttons that open the system browser Menu Slide-over drawer, closes on backdrop, Back or swipe left Sidebar overlay with Escape and backdrop Offline Banner "Content may be out of date" until an offline cache exists n/a Crash Friendly error boundary with Try again error.js pages

docs.title: URL conventions
docs.text: School and question URLs use UUIDs as the lookup key and may append a human-readable slug, for example /schools/{id}/{slug} and /questions/{id}/{slug}. The slug is cosmetic and may be omitted. schoolUrl() and questionUrl() keep links consistent on web. Mobile looks up by id and builds share links with the same pattern.

docs.title: What not to build yet
docs.text:
• School reviews or ratings
  • School verification badges or "claim your school" flows
  • Subscription or payment UI
  • A public API developer portal

If review or monetization work is designed later, paid features must never hide or suppress legitimate negative reviews.

• [x] Curated database of Nigerian universities, polytechnics, and colleges, sourced primarily from NUC, NBTE, and NCCE official lists, cross-referenced against JAMB's institution list and secondary sources. This is the first of what may become several country-specific data pipelines as Academia Atlas expands.

SchoolSourceRecord model added alongside for per-regulator provenance tracking. Schema, serializers, views (three new List Schools filters), and admin all landed. Consuming a real cleaned NUC/NBTE/NCCE dataset via an import command is still pending, tracked separately below.

  • [x] /my-reports page (GET /reports/mine/): the reporter's own reports with status, review date and a link to the content. Private, never on the profile, noindex plus a robots disallow, linked from ProfileMenu.
  • [x] Schools manager Active, Inactive and All tabs (GET /schools/?is_active=), inactive rows carry a visible badge, toggling a row out of the current tab removes it and fixes the count. Failed "View more" now shows an error.
  • [x] Hub offline control for admins (PATCH /hubs/{id}/) in the Hub teams tab, with a confirmation for taking a hub offline. The picker now searches all schools so an offline hub can be found and restored.

docs.title: Monetization (Future. Needs further review)
docs.text: Every item here must hold to Integrity Over Monetization (project-plan.md): paid tiers affect visibility, promotion, and verification only, never the truthfulness or presence of content students post. - [ ] Verified badge and official review response (already scoped under School Verification & Claiming and School Reviews above) - [ ] Directory placement: a school can pay to appear higher specifically in the school directory browse view, clearly labeled "Featured", never affecting search relevance or question ranking - [ ] Analytics dashboard for school representatives: what students are asking about their school, trending unanswered topics, volume over time, business intelligence that's already a byproduct of the platform, genuinely useful to a school, doesn't touch what students see - [ ] Scoped official announcements: a paying school can pin a clearly labeled banner inside their own hub only (e.g. "Registration closes March 30"), doesn't affect any other school or any organic question - [ ] Careers/classifieds section: paid, clearly labeled listings from employers or recruiters targeting specific schools or departments, a natural extension given SIWES and internships are already common organic topics, doesn't compete with organic Q&A content - [ ] Tiered public API access: free low-volume tier plus a paid higher-volume tier for third-party developers wanting bulk access to the curated Nigerian school directory, monetizes the data-curation work directly (see Public/Developer API below) - [ ] Voluntary support ("tip jar" style), optional, transparent about what it funds, never gates any feature

docs.title: Long List Handling (Future)
docs.text:
• [ ] Windowed "View more" lists (Facebook-style). The View more button stays, but only a fixed number of rows ever stay on the page. After the reader has loaded several pages, the oldest rows at the top are dropped from the page, however many times View more is clicked.

    Why: today every click appends a page and nothing is ever removed. After ten clicks a list holds 200 or more rows, which means a large DOM, a scrollbar thumb the size of a pixel, and sluggish scrolling on cheap phones, which this audience uses.

    Behaviour: - Keep a window of N pages (for example 3 pages of 20 rows). When appending another page would exceed it, the oldest page leaves the DOM and a spacer of the same total height takes its place, so the scroll position does not jump. - When the reader scrolls back up to the spacer, a "Show earlier questions" control brings the previous page back and drops a page from the bottom. It can be button-only at first. - Fetched pages stay in an in-memory map keyed by page number, so returning to an earlier page is instant and never refetches. A filter, search or sort change clears the window and the map. - Rows vary in height (the meta row wraps), so measure rows with ResizeObserver and sum the measured heights for the spacer, with an estimate for rows never measured.

    Plan, in this order: 1. Measure first, with 500 realistic rows (React Profiler, Lighthouse). 2. Try CSS only: content-visibility: auto with contain-intrinsic-size on each row skips rendering offscreen rows without removing them. Stop here if that is enough. 3. Build a shared usePagedList hook that owns fetch, append, the stale-response guard and the load-more error, which is logic now hand-copied across about a dozen components. Then a WindowedList wrapper that does the eviction. Adopting the hook is a clean-up on its own.

    Where: RecentQuestionsList, HubQuestionList, TagQuestionsClient, SearchResultsClient, the notifications page, the profile tabs, and the admin lists (users, schools, tags, reports, unanswered queue).

    Details to get right: - Accessibility: announce the position ("Showing 41 to 100 of 340") in a polite live region, never evict a row that holds keyboard focus, and keep the View more button reachable. - Browser find (Ctrl+F) only sees rows currently on the page, so say so. - Do not replay the stagger animation for rows brought back at the top. - Browser Back should restore position: keep the loaded pages and scroll offset in sessionStorage, keyed by route and filters. - The total count in the list header stays the API's count.

    Not goals: classic full-list virtualization, any new dependency, or any change to the API's pagination.

    Done when: after 500 rows are loaded by repeated View more, the DOM never holds more than N rows, scroll position does not jump on eviction, going back to earlier rows works without refetching, the position is announced, and a filter change resets the window.

docs.text:
• [ ] A slim, dismissible AppPromoBanner on mobile browsers only. Never a full page interstitial, which Google penalizes and which blocks content. Hidden on /admin, /moderation and the ask and edit forms, and hidden inside the app. Dismissal remembered for 30 days in localStorage (try/catch). Env gated: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAY_STORE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_IOS_APP_ID. When unset it renders nothing, so it can ship before launch.

Needs the Apple team id and the Android signing fingerprint from the store builds.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
• [x] Private "my reports" view: GET /reports/mine/, self-scoped, shows only the reporter's own reports with status and a link to the content, never reviewer identity or escalation state, so reporting stays private in both directions
  • [x] Hub activation rejection reason is now persisted (HubActivationRequest.rejection_reason) and shown in the admin request list, previously emailed and discarded
  • [x] Admin action audit log (who resolved which report, who suspended which user)
  • [x] Admin action audit log also covers tag merge and delete actions (via AdminActionLog)
  • [ ] Answer edit history, so a heavily-edited answer's original context isn't lost framed as quality signal, not a leaderboard or engagement mechanic, consistent with Knowledge Over Social Activity
  • [x] Standalone answer/comment permalink page, so notifications and reports targeting an answer or comment (VOTE, NEW_COMMENT, non-question reports) can deep-link somewhere real instead of rendering as non-clickable text.
  • [x] UserSerializer's stats field, currently only attached ad hoc in MeView, should become a proper SerializerMethodField on the serializer itself, so it's included everywhere UserSerializer is used (this also closes a real doc/code mismatch, api-contract.md documents stats as present on the Google Login response, but it currently isn't)
  • [x] Google-authenticated users should have set_unusable_password() called explicitly at creation, currently left at Django's blank default, harmless today but worth hardening before email/password auth ships
  • [x] GoogleLoginView should explicitly reject login for suspended (is_active=False) accounts with a clear error, rather than issuing a token pair that only fails on the next authenticated request
  • [x] PATCH /users/me/ should validate full_name isn't blank/whitespace-only and return a proper field error, instead of silently no-op'ing
  • [x] GET /users/search/ should share the existing "search" throttle scope (60/min) rather than falling back to the general 100/min limit, it's a type-ahead endpoint and will be called more rapidly than that implies
  • [x] Google login should verify email_verified from Google's userinfo response before creating/logging in a user, currently trusted implicitly
  • [x] Cache invalidation gap: PATCH /schools/{id}/, POST department creation, and PATCH department updates all invalidate school-detail and/or school-list but never school-by-slug, so slug-based lookups can serve stale data (including a deactivated school still appearing active) for up to CACHE_TTL_MEDIUM after a write. apps.hubs already does this correctly for hub-by-slug, apps.schools needs the same fix
  • [x] SchoolBySlugView lets platform admins read inactive schools and bypasses cached slug results; non-admins see only active schools. School URLs use UUIDs as the lookup key with an optional cosmetic slug, as documented in design-guide.md
  • [x] Shared "is this request from a platform admin" check duplicated across SchoolListCreateView, SchoolDetailView, and inlined again in DepartmentListCreateView.get(), should be a single helper in apps.core.permissions
  • [x] GET /schools/ has no is_active filter for admins, who currently see active and inactive schools in one combined list with no way to narrow to just one, AdminUserListView already has this exact pattern for users, worth matching here
  • [x] Several write endpoints have no dedicated throttle scope and fall back to the general 100/min limit: School/Department creation, Answer edit/delete (AnswerDetailView), Mark Best Answer, Comment edit/delete (CommentDetailView), and Static Page creation (StaticPageListCreateView.post). Worth a deliberate pass deciding which of these actually need tighter scoping versus being fine on the general limit, rather than the current case-by-case inconsistency
  • [x] Hub deactivation endpoint (admin only), mirroring School's soft-delete pattern. Currently no API path exists to take an active hub offline, is_active on Hub can only ever be set to True through the API today
  • [x] If Hub deactivation is added, HubDetailView/HubBySchoolView/ HubBySlugView need the same admin-bypass-for-inactive pattern SchoolDetailView already has, otherwise a deactivated hub becomes unreachable even to the admin who deactivated it
  • [x] Cache invalidation gap (combined with the school-by-slug finding from the Schools audit): approving a hub activation request changes School.has_hub but never invalidates school-by-slug:{slug}, so a school's slug-based lookup can show stale has_hub for up to CACHE_TTL_MEDIUM after activation. Fixed through the shared invalidate_school_cache() helper, used by both apps.schools and apps.hubs so this can't drift again
  • [x] Unanswered questions queue (GET /questions/unanswered/) only checks ModeratorAssignment, not SchoolRepresentativeAssignment, meaning a rep managing a hub with no moderator assigned yet cannot see their own hub's queue at all. Directly inconsistent with the reasoning already applied to NEW_QUESTION's fan-out (widened to include reps for exactly this zero-moderator-hub scenario), same fix belongs here
  • [x] QuestionLockView.check_lock_permission() duplicates hub-role-check logic inline for a third time (Schools and Hubs audits flagged the same pattern already), worth one shared "is moderator or rep for this hub" helper in apps.hubs.permissions instead
  • [x] Django admin's Question list view doesn't surface is_locked, hard to tell which questions are locked without opening each one
  • [x] Search results omit slug (and department, view_count, is_locked) from each question, matching the documented contract exactly today, but meaning the frontend can't build a /questions/{id}/{slug} URL directly from a search result without a follow-up request. Worth deciding whether slug specifically should be added to SearchQuestionSerializer
  • [x] Static Pages endpoints (list and detail) have no caching, unlike Schools/Hubs/Tags which all use the same short-TTL public-read pattern. Deliberately deferred at build time as non-blocking, worth picking up now that it's a formally tracked item
  • [x] Tag list (GET /tags/) is fully unpaginated by design, reasonable at current volume but a real scaling risk given tags are free-text and community-generated with no curation. Recommend adding standard pagination now while cheap. This IS a breaking response-shape change ({"results": [...]} becomes {count, next, previous, results}), needs to be scoped as a coordinated backend+frontend issue, not a silent backend-only change
  • [x] Tag name (max_length=50) is never validated for length before hitting the database on either write path (TagMergeView's rename branch, and _sync_tags() in apps/questions/serializers.py, the implicit tag-creation path any authenticated user hits via question tagging). A name over 50 characters currently raises an unhandled DB-level error instead of a clean 400. Reachable by any regular user, not just admins, worth prioritizing
  • [x] Django admin's Tag list doesn't surface question_count (would need an admin method since it's computed, not a model field)
  • [x] Resolving a report with DELETE_CONTENT can orphan other pending reports pointing at content that gets cascade-deleted along with it (e.g. a Question's report deletes it, cascading to an Answer that had its own separate pending report). Already handled defensively (won't crash), but nothing surfaces or auto-resolves these dangling reports
  • [x] Consider notifying the original reporter when their report is resolved or rejected, matching the "close the loop" pattern already used elsewhere in the notification system, not currently required by any doc but a natural fit
  • [x] GET /reports/ only supports a status filter, adding a content_type filter (question/answer/comment) would let admins scope their review more precisely
  • [x] generate_unique_slug() has a TOCTOU race: the uniqueness check and the eventual save() aren't atomic, so two genuinely simultaneous creates with colliding names could both pass the check and the second save() would raise an uncaught IntegrityError (raw 500) instead of a clean error. Narrow edge case, but worth a retry-on-collision fix before real concurrent traffic exists
  • [x] .env.example documents discrete DATABASE_NAME/USER/PASSWORD/HOST/PORT vars as a fallback when DATABASE_URL is unset, but base.py's actual DATABASES config only ever reads DATABASE_URL via env.db(), those five vars are dead and unused. If DATABASE_URL is left unset while only the discrete vars are configured, the app silently falls back to local SQLite with no warning, a real risk on first deploy. Needs a decision: restore genuine discrete-var fallback logic, or remove the misleading vars from .env.example and document DATABASE_URL as the only path
  • [ ] STORAGES["default"]: now overridable via DEFAULT_FILE_STORAGE_BACKEND but still FileSystemStorage. A cloud backend must be installed and verified against Django 6 before any upload feature ships (Supabase S3-compatible storage via django-storages is the first candidate)
  • [x] DRF's browsable HTML API renderer isn't restricted to JSON-only in production, minor hardening, mostly informational exposure rather than a real vulnerability
  • [x] DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES is globally AllowAny, a deliberate and reasonable choice for this platform, but worth keeping in mind as a standing discipline point: any future view that omits permission_classes is open-by-default, not closed-by-default

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
• [x] lucide-react is pinned to ^1.23.0 in package.json, every prior known release of this library uses a 0.x scheme. Not currently breaking anything (icons render, builds pass), but worth confirming via npm ls lucide-react whether this is a genuine 1.0 release or a typo, and spot-checking that no icon names changed if it's the former
  • [x] TopBar's "Academia Atlas" wordmark is plain text, not a link, inconsistent with Sidebar's identical-looking wordmark which does navigate home. TopBar is the persistently visible one, worth making it a Link too
  • [x] No centralized z-index scale, ad hoc values (TopBar z-30, sidebar backdrop z-40, sidebar/ProfileMenu dropdown both z-50, NavigationProgressBar z-[100]) risk collisions as more overlays are added. Worth a small shared constants pass before that happens
  • [x] Minor accessibility gaps in the shell layer: the mobile sidebar backdrop is a bare div with onClick, no keyboard equivalent or button semantics; ThemeToggle's button doesn't expose aria-pressed for its current state. Cheap, low-risk, worth doing together
  • [x] Establish a lint or PR-review convention preventing route-shaped files from landing inside components/ (or component files landing inside app/), found two real instances of this during the shell audit (see Project_audit_notes.md), worth preventing recurrence now that contributors are regularly opening PRs
  • [x] Both auth-related Route Handlers (app/api/backend/auth/google/route.js's backend fetch, and the token refresh call inside the catch-all [...path]/route.js) have no try/catch around the backend network call itself, only around bad response handling. If the backend is genuinely unreachable rather than just erroring, these throw an unhandled exception that surfaces as a raw Next.js 500 instead of the app's normal error handling. Same gap in two places, worth fixing together
  • [x] lib/jwt.js's decodeJwtExp uses Buffer, Node-runtime-only. Not an active bug (these routes default to the Node runtime), but would need atob/TextDecoder instead if any auth route is ever moved to the Edge runtime
  • [~] Concurrent-request refresh race, formally consolidated here from BUILD_LOG_FRONTEND.md's Known Deviations: if multiple requests expire at the same moment, more than one may attempt to use the same refresh token before rotation completes, one could be rejected. Mitigated within a single instance by the shared refresh promise and grace window; cross-instance races remain. Unlikely at MVP traffic levels
  • [x] RecentQuestionsList's and the search page's handleLoadMore now drop responses that arrive after unmount or after the filter changed. Load more failures are now shown (RecentQuestionsList stored them but never displayed them).
  • [x] Tag list pagination: /tags browse uses load-more, TagsManager can reach, merge and delete tags past the first 50, tag autocomplete, the search tag filter and the merge control request page_size=10, and sitemap.js walks every page of tags.
  • [x] Sitemap lists canonical slugged school URLs and walks every page of schools, tags and questions through one helper that keeps partial results on failure.
  • [x] TagsManager no longer replaces its search bar with a skeleton while loading, which dropped focus on every debounced search.
  • [x] Theme toggle moved from the sidebar footer to an icon button in the TopBar beside the notification bell.
  • [x] Profile page: identity card (avatar, inline name edit, role chips, moderation link, stats strip) above one tab strip (Activity, Questions, Answers, Comments). Tabs stay mounted once opened.
  • [x] Admin hub picker shows its "no hub yet" message under the school that was picked, and rows show an opening state.
  • [x] Question detail's "back to school" link now routes directly via schoolUrl() instead of through the /hubs/{id} redirect hop. QuestionHubSchoolSerializer gained an id field, additive, needed for the link to be buildable at all.
  • [x] Meta-row pattern (small icon + label, e.g. author/department/views on question detail, "by {author}" on answers and comments) has been copy-pasted across multiple files with drifting icon sizes relative to their adjacent text (16px icons next to 11-14px text in a few places, now hand-corrected where found during the audit). Worth extracting into one shared component (e.g. a small IconLabel) so icon-to-text proportion stays consistent by construction instead of needing to be independently gotten right in every new usage
  • [x] border-gray-200 dark:border-gray-700 (Tailwind's literal gray scale) still appears in place of border-[var(--color-border)] (the project's actual warm-neutral border token) in at least HubQuestionList and app/tags/[name]/page.js's list containers, found independently in two different passes of this audit, likely present elsewhere too. Worth one project-wide search-and-fix rather than continuing to patch individual instances as they're found
  • [x] NotificationBell's dropdown only ever fetches once per session (toggle() skips refetching once status leaves "idle"), so both the notification list and its own unread count go stale after the first open, a new notification arriving mid-session won't show up, in the list or the badge, until a full page reload. Worth a deliberate decision on the right fix (refetch on every open, a periodic poll, or something event-driven) rather than picking one blind
  • [x] ReportButton's modal uses raw border-gray-300 dark:border-gray-600 instead of border-[var(--color-border)], the only modal shell in the app still on the un-tokenized value, RequestHubModal already uses the token correctly. Small, fix opportunistically
  • [x] Filter sidebar (FilterSidebar, shared across HubQuestionList, search, and tag question lists) stacks above the results list on mobile by default grid behavior, meaning a mobile visitor has to scroll past the entire filter panel before seeing any question. Worth a collapsible/toggle treatment on narrow screens, one shared component fix covers all three usages
  • [ ] Hub offline notice for moderators and representatives: needs a backend change first (keep offline hubs in moderator_for and representative_for with a hub_active flag, plus HUB_DEACTIVATED and HUB_REACTIVATED notifications), then a banner on /moderation.
  • [x] Empty states across the app are plain gray text ("No questions yet.", "No comments yet.", etc.) with no visual weight. A small shared EmptyState component (icon + message + optional call-to-action) would read as more intentional and could be dropped in everywhere at once rather than each spot staying ad hoc
  • [x] Form inputs, selects and textareas ... restyled onto Input, Select and Textarea by the same codemod for every control carrying the standard styling. The ask and edit question forms, the answer form, the department form and the request-hub modal are fully converted with FormField (label tied to control, inline field errors through lib/formErrors.js).
  • [ ] Labels on SchoolFormModal and PageFormModal (label wiring for these two remaining forms)
  • [x] Error and warning messages are ad hoc red paragraphs ... moved to the shared ErrorMessage by scripts/codemod-primitives.mjs, with the three error.js boundary pages left as they were.
  • [x] No persistent "Ask a question" affordance on mobile. AskFab, a floating Ask button below the sm breakpoint for signed-in users, hidden on the ask and edit forms and on /admin and /moderation.
  • [x] Muted secondary text contrast: measured, text-gray-400 failed in light mode (about 2.5:1) and text-gray-500 in dark mode (about 3.7:1). A text-muted utility (light #67645C, dark #9EA1AB, at least 4.5:1 on every surface the app uses) replaced both across the app.
  • [x] Static page editor word and character count (richMode only). The other markdown editor ideas (grouped undo, paste-to-link, nested lists, auto-closing markers) stay deferred.
  • [ ] Further markdown editor optimizations to consider, none urgent, worth scoping individually before picking any up:
  • Undo/redo that understands formatting actions as single steps (e.g. one Ctrl+Z fully removes a toolbar-applied bold wrap) rather than relying purely on the browser textarea's native undo stack, which can split one logical action across several undo steps
  • Paste handling: auto-converting a pasted raw URL into [text](url) when text is selected at paste time, matching the interaction model of most modern editors
  • Tab/Shift+Tab to indent and outdent list items (nested lists), currently list items are always flat, no indentation support in either the editor shortcuts or the renderer's allowed output
  • A visible character/word count for static pages specifically, useful there in a way it isn't for short Q&A content (added to the rich mode attribute)
  • Auto-closing bracket/marker pairs while typing (typing ** inserts the closing ** automatically with the cursor between them), a genuinely bigger behavioral change worth a deliberate look at edge cases (nested formatting, existing text after the cursor) rather than a quick addition
  • [x] Forms: labels are tied to their fields on the ask, edit, answer, department, request-hub, report and escalate forms and the school filters. (SchoolFormModal and PageFormModal still open, see above.)
  • [ ] A shared Modal primitive. Every dialog (report, escalate, school form, page form, request hub) repeats the same backdrop and has no dialog semantics, Escape-to-close or focus handling.

docs.title: Mobile Client (mobile)
docs.text: Expo (React Native, TypeScript) user client for iOS and Android. It calls the Django API directly, with tokens in secure storage and no web proxy. mobile-map.md says where the code lives. Area headings match the Frontend Capabilities section so the two compare line by line. Legend as above. Each line ends with a parity tag after a pipe: "parity", "differs: reason" or "gap: what is missing on mobile". docs.title: Differs from web (by design)
docs.text:
• User client only: no moderation or admin screens, staff open the web app in the system browser, no tokens in the URL
  • Tokens in secure storage, direct API calls, single-flight refresh, no Next.js proxy
  • Native Google account picker instead of Google Identity Services
  • Bottom tabs plus drawer, bottom sheets instead of modals and dropdowns, filters as chips and a sheet
  • Comment actions, report and escalate forms live inside one sheet, no stacked modals
  • Platform badge explanation opens in a sheet (inline inside the comments sheet) instead of a popover
  • Search rows show only the fields the search endpoint returns
  • No windowed lists and no hub-offline banner (also open on the web)
  • Offline content cache and push notifications are not built (future)

docs.title: Web Map
docs.text: A file-by-file mental model of web/, for anyone (or any chat) picking up web work. It answers "where does it live". For "what can it do" read the Web Capabilities section of feature-list.md, for the API read api-contract.md, for visual rules read design-guide.md, and for history and decisions read BUILD_LOG_FRONTEND.md.

docs.title: 1. Stack and tooling
docs.text:
• Next.js 16 App Router (Turbopack), React 19, JavaScript (no TypeScript), Tailwind v4 (CSS-first, no tailwind.config.js), lucide-react 1.23 icons, marked plus sanitize-html for Markdown, Plus Jakarta Sans through next/font (self-hosted). No third-party component library.
  • Deployed on Vercel. The browser never talks to Django directly.
Script What it does npm run dev, build, start Standard Next.js scripts npm run lint ESLint (two rules are off on purpose, see eslint.config.mjs) npm run check:structure scripts/check-structure.mjs: no route files outside app/, no component files inside app/, every lucide icon name must exist npm run check lint plus structure check. Run npm run check && npm run build before every PR scripts/codemod-primitives.mjs One-off migration to ErrorMessage and the form controls. Dry run by default, --write applies. Safe to re-run

docs.title: 2. Environment variables
docs.text:
Name Where Consumers Purpose BACKEND_API_URL server only app/api/backend routes Backend /api/v1 base, no trailing slash NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL build and server lib/api.js, metadata, sitemap, robots, OG Public origin, also used for server calls to the app's own proxy NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID browser GoogleLoginButton Google Identity Services client id NEXT_PUBLIC_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT_ID browser lib/platformAccount.js Comma-separated user ids that get the platform badge (optional)

NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are baked in at build time, so changing one needs a redeploy.

docs.title: 3. Architecture and data flow
docs.text:
Browser -> Next route handler /api/backend/[...path] -> Django /api/v1/...
  • Tokens live only in httpOnly cookies, never in browser-readable code. The route handler attaches Authorization, retries once after a refresh and rotates the cookies.
  • Refresh: lib/refreshSession.js keeps one in-flight refresh per refresh token and remembers the result for 10 seconds, so concurrent 401s share one refresh. Cookies are cleared only on a definitive 400 or 401 from the refresh endpoint, never on 429, 5xx or a network failure. Backend unreachable returns 503 { "error": ... }.
  • Client components call clientFetch (lib/clientApi.js). It throws an Error carrying status, fields (the raw DRF body) and friendly copy for network failure, 429 and gateway errors.
  • Server components call apiFetch (lib/api.js), which forwards the request cookies to the app's own proxy through NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL.
  • Events: a 401 anywhere dispatches auth:expired and AuthProvider logs the UI out. lib/locationEvents.js patches history.pushState and replaceState to emit app:locationchange, because a Next <Link> that only changes the hash fires neither hashchange nor popstate.
  • Known limits: a race between two serverless instances can cause a stray logout, and a token refresh during a server render cannot reach the browser until its next request.

docs.title: 8. Permissions on the client
docs.text:
• Roles come from useAuth().user: is_admin, moderator_for[], representative_for[] (hub_id plus school). Hiding a control is UX only, the backend enforces everything.
  • canEscalate(user, hubId) in EscalateButton.js is the one check for escalation. Lock, moderation tabs and department management derive from the same fields.
  • refreshUser() must run after an admin changes a hub's status, because /users/me/ lists only active hubs.

docs.title: 9. Conventions
docs.text:
• Lists: status loading | ready | error, first page in an effect with a cancel or request-id guard, "View more" appends (dedupe by id when order can shift), load-more errors shown under the button, empty state through EmptyState, count line "N things".
  • Forms: FormField plus Input, Select or Textarea (label tied to control, inline error). Backend field errors through fieldErrorsFrom. No raw red paragraphs, use ErrorMessage.
  • Modals (Report, Escalate, SchoolForm, PageForm, RequestHub) are controlled, z-modal, with no shared Modal primitive yet.
  • Tokens: --color-border dividers, --color-border-strong controls, text-muted for all secondary text (never text-gray-400 or 500), --color-accent #3454D1. Stacking utilities: z-dropdown 20, z-sticky 30, z-overlay 40, z-drawer 50, z-modal 60, z-toast 70, z-progress 100. Never raw z numbers. See design-guide.md.
  • Client API: always clientFetch, never fetch to the backend from the browser.

docs.title: 10. Behaviours that are easy to get wrong
docs.text:
• SOLVED means "has a best answer". Only is_locked blocks new answers.
  • Question and school URLs are UUID plus a cosmetic slug, the slug is never used for lookup.
  • Notification and report links come from link_target, null means no link.
  • Reports are private: /my-reports only, never on the profile, never reviewer or escalation data.
  • router.refresh() updates server props but never resets a client component's own state, reset loading state explicitly after a success.

docs.title: 11. How to add things
docs.text:
• New page: file under app/, metadata through export const metadata or generateMetadata. If it needs client state, make a thin server wrapper plus a client component.
  • New list: copy HubQuestionList's loading pattern, use EmptyState and ErrorMessage.
  • New API call: through clientFetch (client) or apiFetch (server).
  • New icon: import from lucide-react, npm run check:structure verifies the name.
  • New notification type: add its icon to the NotificationItem icon map, and to the mobile client.

docs.title: 12. Known gaps
docs.text: See "Known gaps" in the Web Capabilities section of feature-list.md: hub-offline notice for moderators (needs backend), shared Modal primitive, label wiring in SchoolFormModal and PageFormModal, windowed "View more" lists, and optional stronger control borders.

docs.title: 13. Keeping this file current
docs.text:
Regenerate the tree and exports after any file move, new route or new shared primitive:

find app components lib scripts -type f \( -name "*.js" -o -name "*.mjs" \) | sort

docs.text:
• React Native 0.88.1, React 19.3.0, Expo SDK ~58, TypeScript ~6.0.3. Navigation: React Navigation 7 (native stack, bottom tabs) plus a custom slide-over drawer. Icons: FontAwesome6 through @expo/vector-icons. Font: Plus Jakarta Sans 400 to 800 (@expo-google-fonts/plus-jakarta-sans).

  • Builds: eas.json has development, preview (APK) and production profiles. The env block of a profile holds the public EXPO_PUBLIC_* values, EAS never reads .env.
Script What it does npm start, android, ios, web Expo dev server (npx expo start -c clears the cache) npm run typecheck tsc --noEmit npm run export:web Production web export check npx expo-doctor Dependency and config health npx expo export --platform android Proves the JS bundles (pre-flight before a build) npx expo prebuild --platform android --no-install --clean Validates app.json and config plugins, then rm -rf android brand/make-brand-assets.sh Generates every icon, splash and brand PNG (repo root)

Name Consumer Purpose EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL src/api/config.ts API base including /api/v1. Derived from the Metro host when blank (Expo Go). Required in builds EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_BASE_URL src/config/app.ts Share links and the staff web handoff EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID, EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID src/auth/GoogleSignInButton.tsx Web OAuth client, used for web sign in and to configure the native library EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID GoogleSignInButton.tsx iOS client (iOS untested) EXPO_PUBLIC_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT_ID src/config/app.ts Comma separated user ids that get the official "A" badge (per database) EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL src/config/app.ts Shown with the suspended-account message EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_MODE src/config/app.ts Developer access sheet, honoured only when __DEV__ EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_ACCESS_TOKEN, _REFRESH_TOKEN AuthProvider.tsx Optional seeded dev login, __DEV__ only

docs.title: 3. Architecture and data flow
docs.text:
• Direct API. The app calls Django at /api/v1 with no proxy. Native requests have no CORS. src/api/client.ts attaches the bearer token to every request (also public reads, so user_vote and is_following are personalised), enforces timeouts, and turns failures into ApiError (status, fields, network).
  • Session. Tokens live in expo-secure-store (localStorage on web). A 401 triggers one shared refresh. The session is cleared only on a definitive 400 or 401 from /auth/refresh/. Network failure, 429 and 5xx keep the session and start from the cached user.
  • Guests and the auth gate. Guests browse freely. requireAuth(action) opens one sign-in sheet that keeps the screen and resumes the action after login. The Login screen is a one-time welcome.
  • Roles. useCapabilities() is the only place roles are derived. Hiding a control is UX, the backend enforces everything. The mobile client has no moderation or admin screens: staff get lock, report and escalate in context and "Open on web" handoffs that never carry a token.
  • Lists. usePagedList (paged, deduped, stale-guarded, pull to refresh, View more with its own error). useQuery for single resources.
  • Google. Native: Google account picker, access token to POST /auth/google/. Web: browser token flow.

docs.title: 13. Conventions
docs.text:
1. Lists: usePagedList, FlatList with RefreshControl, ViewMoreButton in the footer, skeleton while loading, EmptyState when empty, ErrorState with retry.
  2. Forms: Field plus fieldError(err, name). Never show raw error objects.
  3. Sheets over modal screens. Never stack Modals: switch the content of one sheet by mode.
  4. Colours only through useTheme() tokens, never hex (white on accent excepted).
  5. Roles only through useCapabilities().
  6. Restricted actions through requireAuth, never a redirect to Login.
  7. Screens with inputs wrap in KeyboardAvoid, keyboard state only from useKeyboard.
  8. Reuse: a block used twice, or one that pushes a screen past a few hundred lines, becomes a component.
  9. User content only through Markdown and MarkdownEditor, new formatting goes in lib/markdownEdit.ts.
  10. Author names always carry PlatformBadge.
  11. Suggestion lists render inline under the field, not as popovers.
  12. Reports through ReportForm only.
  13. No em dash characters in code, comments or docs.

docs.title: 14. Behaviours that are easy to get wrong
docs.text:
• SOLVED means "has a best answer". Only is_locked blocks new answers. Only the question author marks best.
  • Reports are private: /my-reports only, no reviewer or escalation data, never on the profile.
  • Notification and report links come from link_target, null means no link.
  • A failed refresh must not log the user out unless it was a definitive 400 or 401.
  • Vote switching updates the UI after each confirmed server step.
  • Heading syntax renders as plain text everywhere except static pages.
  • Preview and production builds contain no developer sheet and no seeded tokens (__DEV__).
